questions.stem: How many challenges of risk management are identified in the lecture note?
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies four challenges of risk management: difficulty in predicting future events, lack of risk management expertise, limited financial resources, and poor project planning.

questions.stem: A project that fails to meet standards has poor:
questions.explanation: Deliverables that do not satisfy specs reflect poor quality[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines a project?

options.A: A permanent organisational function carried out by a dedicated department
options.B: A temporary activity undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result within a specified time frame using limited resources
options.C: A routine operational task repeated at regular intervals to sustain business output
options.D: A long-term strategic plan developed by senior management for organisational growth

questions.explanation: A project is defined as a temporary activity with specific objectives and limited resources aimed at producing a unique product, service, or result - distinguishing it from ongoing operational work.

questions.stem: The total float could be calculated using one of the formulas:
questions.explanation: Total float is defined as Latest Start minus Earliest Start ($LS - ES$) or Latest Finish minus Earliest Finish ($LF - EF$)[cite: 4].

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic that every project must have?
questions.explanation: Projects always operate within limited resources - time, money, manpower, and materials. An unlimited budget contradicts the fundamental constraint of limited resources inherent in every project.

questions.stem: Which three elements form the "Iron Triangle" of project management?
questions.explanation: The Iron Triangle (triple constraints) consists of Scope, Time, and Cost[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a project?
questions.explanation: Construction of a school building is a temporary, unique activity with a definite start and end, specific objectives, and defined resources - all hallmarks of a project. The other options are routine, ongoing operations.

questions.stem: Which is NOT a step in project evaluation?
questions.explanation: Increasing budgets is a financial administration task, not a step in evaluating a project[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Organizing a seminar or workshop is classified as a project primarily because it is:

options.A: Carried out by a large number of people
options.B: A temporary, unique activity with defined objectives and a set time frame
options.D: A recurring monthly activity in most organisations

questions.explanation: Organising a seminar qualifies as a project because it has a clear start and end, specific goals, and defined resources - the core elements that distinguish a project from routine work.

questions.stem: A stakeholder analysis in evaluation helps identify:

options.A: Interests and influence of key parties

questions.explanation: Stakeholder analysis determines key parties, their interests, and their degree of influence[cite: 2].

questions.stem: The characteristic of 'temporariness' in project management means that:

options.A: Projects are always completed in less than one week
options.B: Every project has a definite starting and finishing date
options.C: Projects are only carried out during a particular season of the year
options.D: Project teams are dissolved before work begins

questions.explanation: Temporariness refers to the fact that every project has a defined beginning and end - it is not an ongoing operation. The duration may vary widely, but the existence of both a start and a finish date is non-negotiable.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key purpose of team-building activities?
questions.explanation: Team-building builds personal rapport, improves communication, and develops trust[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which project characteristic explains why no two projects are exactly alike?
questions.explanation: Uniqueness is the characteristic that states each project produces a unique product or service. Even if two projects appear similar, differences in context, stakeholders, or environment make each one distinct.

questions.stem: A communication plan outlines:
questions.explanation: The communication plan defines who receives project status updates, how often, and through which channels[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project operates under constraints of time, money, manpower, and materials. This characteristic is known as:
questions.explanation: The limited resources characteristic highlights that projects must be executed within defined boundaries of time, budget, personnel, and materials - making efficient resource management critical.

questions.stem: What might cause a project to fail the feasibility study?
questions.explanation: Lack of required financial, human, or technical resources will cause a project to fail feasibility[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which characteristic of a project acknowledges that unforeseen events may affect its success?
questions.explanation: Risk and uncertainty is the characteristic that recognises projects involve unknowns that could threaten their success, which is why risk management is a vital part of project management.

questions.stem: One pitfall in project evaluation is:
questions.explanation: Ignoring feedback limits institutional learning and leads to repeating previous mistakes[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project team is assembled to construct a community health centre. The team is given a budget and a 12-month deadline. Which project characteristic is demonstrated by the 12-month deadline?
questions.explanation: The 12-month deadline defines a clear finishing point for the project, which is the essence of the temporariness characteristic - every project has a definite start and end.

questions.stem: What typically occurs during the "Storming" stage of team development?

options.A: Team members establish trust and cohesion

questions.explanation: Storming is characterized by interpersonal friction, role confusion, and power struggles[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Project management is best described as:

options.A: The hiring and training of staff to execute organisational tasks
options.B: The application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to plan, organise, direct, and control project activities
options.C: The daily supervision of employees in a corporate organisation
options.D: The financial auditing of project expenditures at the end of a project

questions.explanation: Project management is formally defined as applying knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to plan, organise, direct, and control project activities in order to achieve project objectives effectively and efficiently.

questions.stem: Which criterion assesses if the project met its deadlines?
questions.explanation: Schedule performance checks adherence to project time lines and deadlines[cite: 2].

questions.stem: In simple terms, project management ensures that the right work is done at the right time, within budget, and with:
questions.explanation: Project management is summarised as ensuring the right work is done at the right time, within budget, and with expected quality - covering the triple constraints of time, cost, and quality.

questions.stem: Which document would you update when encountering scope changes?
questions.explanation: When scope changes are formally approved, the scope baseline is updated[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an objective of project management?

options.C: Maximise the number of project stakeholders

questions.explanation: The objectives of project management focus on achieving goals, meeting schedules, controlling costs, efficient resource use, quality, risk reduction, and team coordination. Maximising stakeholders is not among them.

questions.stem: Risk management includes:
questions.explanation: Risk management consists of identifying potential risks, analyzing impacts, and developing mitigation plans[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project manager ensures that her team finishes tasks on schedule, stays within the approved budget, and delivers a standard product. Which objective of project management does this scenario best illustrate?

options.A: Improve coordination among team members only
options.B: Achieve project goals, complete within scheduled time, and control costs
options.C: Reduce the number of team members on the project
options.D: Identify as many stakeholders as possible

questions.explanation: The scenario directly demonstrates three core objectives of project management: achieving goals, completing within scheduled time, and controlling project costs - the classic triple constraints.

questions.stem: During which phase are detailed project plans developed?
questions.explanation: Detailed sub-plans for schedule, cost, quality, and risk are built in the planning phase[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Project management promotes efficient resource utilisation primarily by:

options.A: Hiring more staff than required for any project
options.B: Preventing wastage of materials, time, and funds
options.C: Ensuring all projects are funded by external donors
options.D: Eliminating all forms of teamwork in the organisation

questions.explanation: One key importance of project management is that it promotes efficient resource utilisation by preventing wastage of materials, time, and funds - ensuring every resource is deployed purposefully.

questions.stem: Which activity is part of the execution phase?
questions.explanation: Execution includes performing the actual work, such as coding software or physical development[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which importance of project management relates to providing structured procedures for solving problems?
questions.explanation: Project management improves decision making by providing structured procedures for solving problems, enabling project managers and teams to respond to challenges in an organised, logical manner.

questions.stem: Stakeholder engagement results in:
questions.explanation: Collaborating with varied stakeholders brings diverse ideas and technical insights[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Identifying and managing possible project challenges early is associated with which importance of project management?
questions.explanation: Minimising risk is described as identifying and managing possible project challenges early, allowing the project team to put mitigation measures in place before problems escalate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a principle of project evaluation?
questions.explanation: Avoiding stakeholders directly contradicts the core evaluation principle of active engagement[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Project management improves accountability within a project team by:

options.A: Promoting a flat organisational structure with no defined roles
options.B: Defining responsibilities clearly for each team member
options.C: Allowing every team member to perform all tasks simultaneously
options.D: Removing deadlines to reduce pressure on staff

questions.explanation: Improved accountability is achieved when project management defines responsibilities clearly, so every team member knows what they are expected to deliver and can be held responsible for their outputs.

questions.stem: Baseline data is used to:

options.A: Compare project performance against initial targets

questions.explanation: Baseline data serves as an initial reference point to measure subsequent performance[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a common challenge in project management?
questions.explanation: Scope changes - alterations to the original project requirements - are listed as a common challenge in project management, often leading to cost overruns and schedule delays.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a project charter?
questions.explanation: The project charter officially starts the project and gives authority to the project manager[cite: 3].

questions.stem: How many objectives of project scheduling are identified in the lecture note?
questions.explanation: The lecture lists five objectives of project scheduling: ensuring timely completion, coordinating activities effectively, allocating resources efficiently, monitoring project progress, and identifying possible delays.

questions.stem: Which phase runs concurrently with execution?
questions.explanation: Monitoring and controlling happens alongside execution to ensure the project stays on track[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following PAIRS of importance of project management are correctly matched to their descriptions?

options.A: Encourages teamwork → Prevents wastage of funds; Improves accountability → Promotes collaboration
options.B: Enhances proper planning → Organises activities systematically; Minimises risk → Identifies challenges early
options.C: Ensures goal achievement → Defines responsibilities clearly; Improves decision making → Keeps activities focused
options.D: Promotes resource utilisation → Provides structured problem-solving procedures; Minimises risk → Ensures budget control

questions.explanation: Enhances proper planning means helping organisations organise activities systematically, and minimises risk means identifying and managing possible challenges early - both are accurate pairings from the course material.

questions.stem: Why is the planning phase considered iterative?

options.B: Because plans may need updates as the project progresses

questions.explanation: Planning is progressive and iterative, adapting as clearer information becomes available[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A project manager is primarily responsible for:

options.A: Funding the project from personal savings
options.B: Planning, executing, monitoring, and completing a project
options.C: Marketing the final product to consumers
options.D: Auditing the financial records of the organisation

questions.explanation: A project manager is defined as the person responsible for planning, executing, monitoring, and completing a project - encompassing the entire lifecycle of project delivery.

questions.stem: Stakeholder management focuses on:
questions.explanation: Stakeholder management centers on effective engagement and communication with key parties[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following is among the major responsibilities of a project manager?

options.C: Setting the organisation's vision and mission
options.D: Recruiting permanent staff for the organisation

questions.explanation: Communicating with stakeholders is explicitly listed as a major responsibility of a project manager, ensuring all parties are informed about project progress, changes, and outcomes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key activity in the closing phase?
questions.explanation: Handing over deliverables to the sponsor or customer is a key closeout activity[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Allocating resources and managing risks are responsibilities of:
questions.explanation: Allocating resources and managing risks are both listed as major responsibilities of the project manager, who oversees all aspects of project execution from planning through to completion.

questions.stem: A project charter defines:
questions.explanation: A project charter formally authorizes a project and outlines high-level objectives and authority[cite: 2].

questions.stem: During a road construction project, the supervisor notices that the delivery of gravel has been delayed, threatening the project timeline. Which responsibility of the project manager does addressing this delay fall under?
questions.explanation: A supply delay is a risk to the project timeline. Identifying and addressing it falls under monitoring progress and managing risks - core responsibilities of the project manager.

questions.stem: Which phase ensures deliverables meet quality standards?
questions.explanation: Quality control and assurance check deliverables against quality standards during monitoring and controlling[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a required skill for a successful project manager?
questions.explanation: The skills listed for a project manager include leadership, communication, organisational, problem-solving, time management, decision-making, financial management, and team management skills. Graphic design is not among them.

questions.stem: A project manager's role includes:

options.A: Leading the team and ensuring deliverables

questions.explanation: The PM leads the project team and takes responsibility for delivering results[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project manager who keeps the team motivated, resolves conflicts, and drives performance is demonstrating:
questions.explanation: Motivating teams, resolving conflicts, and driving performance are hallmarks of leadership skills - the first skill listed as required for a successful project manager.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between the planning and execution phases?

options.C: Planning provides the roadmap for execution

questions.explanation: The planning phase produces the baseline roadmap that guides execution[cite: 3].

questions.stem: The ability to manage a project budget, track expenditures, and prevent overspending relates to which skill of a project manager?
questions.explanation: Financial management skills involve handling project budgets, tracking costs, and preventing overspending - critical for keeping a project within its approved financial constraints.

questions.stem: The available time allowed to delay not to the completion time of such task in the network path is:
questions.explanation: Free float is the time an activity can be delayed without delaying the early start of any successor[cite: 4].

questions.stem: Which TWO skills of a project manager work most closely together to ensure project tasks are delegated, tracked, and completed on time?

options.A: Leadership skills and graphic design ability
options.B: Time management skills and organisational skills
options.C: Financial management skills and marketing skills

questions.explanation: Time management skills (ensuring tasks are completed on schedule) and organisational skills (structuring activities and delegating effectively) are closely linked and together drive on-time project delivery.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a stage in conducting a feasibility study?
questions.explanation: A projected income statement is a financial document output rather than a procedural stage of conducting a feasibility study.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an application of project management in education?
questions.explanation: Curriculum development is listed as an application of project management in the education sector, alongside school programme organisation, research projects, and educational seminars.

questions.stem: Management implementation involves:
questions.explanation: Implementation translates evaluation findings and recommendations into strategy execution[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Product development and marketing campaigns are examples of project management applied in:
questions.explanation: Product development and marketing campaigns are explicitly listed as applications of project management in the business sector, alongside business expansion and construction projects.

questions.stem: The aim of stakeholder collaboration is:
questions.explanation: Engaging stakeholders provides broader insights, varied opinions, and stronger project ownership[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A university decides to build a new ICT centre for students. This initiative best falls under project management applied in:
questions.explanation: Development of an ICT centre is given as a project example and falls within the education sector application of project management, which includes school programme organisation and infrastructure development.

questions.stem: A SWOT analysis in evaluation assesses:
questions.explanation: SWOT evaluates internal Strengths and Weaknesses along with external Opportunities and Threats[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project team is unable to meet its deadline because key engineers resigned mid-project. Which challenge does this scenario illustrate?
questions.explanation: The resignation of key engineers represents a lack of skilled personnel - one of the common challenges in project management that can jeopardise project timelines and quality.

questions.stem: What are the three components of the "iron triangle"?
questions.explanation: The Iron Triangle parameters are Scope, Cost, and Time[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Poor planning as a challenge in project management can lead to:

options.A: Surplus resources and early project completion
options.B: Time delays, cost overruns, and goal failure
options.D: Increased stakeholder confidence in the project

questions.explanation: Poor planning is the root cause of many project failures, typically manifesting as time delays, cost overruns, and an inability to meet project goals - making thorough upfront planning essential.

questions.stem: During which phase would you most likely create a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)?
questions.explanation: The WBS is defined during planning to decompose project scope into smaller work items[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which combination of challenges would MOST likely cause a project to fail completely?

options.A: Too many skilled workers and a large budget
options.B: Poor planning, insufficient funds, and poor communication
options.D: Thorough planning and a clearly defined scope

questions.explanation: Poor planning, insufficient funds, and poor communication are all listed challenges in project management; occurring together, they create a compound problem that dramatically raises the risk of total project failure.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a feasibility study in project management?

options.B: To assess the viability of a proposed project

questions.explanation: Feasibility studies analyze whether a project is viable, achievable, and practical[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a project from a routine operation?

options.A: A project is ongoing and repetitive, while a routine operation has a definite end
options.B: A project is temporary and unique, while a routine operation is continuous and repetitive
options.C: A project requires no resources, while a routine operation demands large budgets
options.D: A project is managed by the government, while a routine operation is managed privately

questions.explanation: The key distinction is that projects are temporary (with a defined start and end) and unique (producing something novel), whereas routine operations are ongoing, repetitive activities that sustain the organisation.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the closing phase?

options.B: To formally complete all project activities

questions.explanation: The closing phase ensures all work is completed, contracts are settled, and formal sign-off is granted[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A state government wants to launch a community health campaign. For the campaign to be effectively managed as a project, which element is MOST critical at the outset?

options.A: Hiring a graphic designer to create campaign posters
options.B: Defining clear project objectives, timeline, and resource budget
options.C: Purchasing all materials before setting objectives
options.D: Completing the campaign before informing stakeholders

questions.explanation: Effective project management begins with defining clear objectives, a timeline, and a resource budget - the foundational planning elements that determine the scope and direction of any project.

questions.stem: Cost-benefit analysis evaluates:
questions.explanation: Cost-benefit analysis weighs financial costs against anticipated gains to check viability[cite: 2].

questions.stem: The triple constraint in project management refers to balancing which three elements?
questions.explanation: Project management ensures that work is done at the right time (time), within budget (cost), and with expected quality - the three constraints that must be balanced throughout any project.

questions.stem: Internal evaluation is conducted by:
questions.explanation: Internal evaluations are handled by existing project staff or internal personnel[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following scenarios best illustrates the importance of project management in improving coordination among team members?

options.A: A project manager works alone without involving any team members
options.B: Different departments receive conflicting instructions and miss deadlines
options.C: A project manager assigns clear roles, holds regular meetings, and ensures all units work toward the same goal
options.D: Team members are allowed to set their own individual budgets independently

questions.explanation: Improving coordination involves promoting collaboration - achieved by assigning clear roles, facilitating communication through meetings, and aligning all team efforts toward shared project objectives.

questions.stem: Monitoring & Controlling ensures:

options.A: Project stays on track via KPIs and adjustments

questions.explanation: This phase checks project progress and ensures alignment with goals[cite: 5].

questions.stem: An organisation fails to complete a development project on time and over budget. A review reveals that risks were never identified or planned for. Which importance of project management was neglected?
questions.explanation: The failure to identify and plan for risks is a direct neglect of the 'minimises risk' importance of project management, which states that potential challenges should be identified and managed early.

questions.stem: A project closure report includes:
questions.explanation: A closure report records final outcomes, performance metrics, and official sign-offs[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the primary functions of a project manager?
questions.explanation: A project manager is responsible for planning, executing, monitoring, and completing a project - a sequence that mirrors the standard project lifecycle from initiation to closure.

questions.stem: What happens when you adjust one element of the triple constraints?

options.B: At least one other element must also change

questions.explanation: Because constraints are interrelated, changing one inevitably impacts at least one other element[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following best summarises the core purpose of project management as introduced in AMS 104?

options.A: To maximise profits by reducing the workforce on every project
options.B: To apply knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques so that project objectives are achieved within constraints of time, cost, and quality
options.C: To ensure government agencies approve all project activities before execution
options.D: To eliminate all forms of risk by avoiding new or unique projects

questions.explanation: Project management is defined as the application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to achieve project objectives, ensuring the right work is done at the right time, within budget, and with expected quality - the comprehensive summary of the discipline.

questions.stem: Which action helps mitigate cost constraints?
questions.explanation: Thorough cost estimation and continuous financial tracking help keep projects within budget[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Academic research studies fall under which type of project?
questions.explanation: Academic research studies are explicitly listed as examples of research projects - a distinct project type focused on systematic investigation to generate new knowledge or findings.

questions.stem: For the critical path of the application, a project must satisfy which one of the following conditions: (1) the path must have a defined starting point alone (2) the jobs must have a defined ending point where (3) the path must be continuous (4) calculated from the earliest starting time:
questions.explanation: Network path criteria require defined start/end points and continuous dependency connections throughout[cite: 4].

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most complete definition of a project as covered in Week 2?

options.A: A permanent departmental function designed to sustain daily organisational output
options.B: A planned set of interrelated activities undertaken within a specific period to achieve predetermined objectives using available resources
options.C: A spontaneous activity initiated to address an emergency without prior planning
options.D: A repetitive task carried out continuously by an organisation to meet customer demand

questions.explanation: The Week 2 definition states that a project is a planned set of interrelated activities undertaken within a specific period to achieve predetermined objectives using available resources - emphasising planning, interrelation, time-boundedness, and resource use.

questions.stem: Which constraint would be most affected by adding new features to a software project mid-way?
questions.explanation: Adding deliverables or features directly expands project scope[cite: 3].

questions.stem: According to the scholarly definition introduced in Week 2, a project is:

options.A: A permanent endeavour to create a standard product for mass consumption
options.B: A temporary endeavour undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result
options.C: A budgeted plan for daily organisational operations
options.D: A government-funded initiative for national development

questions.explanation: The scholarly definition presented in Week 2 describes a project as a temporary endeavour undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result - aligning with widely accepted project management literature.

questions.stem: Which method focuses on identifying and managing threats?
questions.explanation: Risk assessment analyzes potential problems and plans steps to mitigate threats[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Projects are usually created to:

options.A: Maintain existing operations without any change
options.B: Solve a problem, meet a need, or improve an existing condition
options.C: Replace all permanent staff in an organisation

questions.explanation: The lecture states that a project is usually created to solve a problem, meet a need, or improve an existing condition - giving it a clear purpose beyond mere routine execution.

questions.stem: Which factor is most critical for phase transitions?
questions.explanation: Phase transitions (phase gates) require explicit formal sign-off before moving to the next stage[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which aspect of the nature of a project explains that every project is designed to accomplish a particular objective?
questions.explanation: Goal-oriented activity is the nature element that states every project is designed to achieve a particular objective, distinguishing it from activities with vague or general purposes.

questions.stem: Project evaluation increases:
questions.explanation: Learning from structured evaluation results leads directly to increased overall performance[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project that requires careful planning before execution is reflecting which element of its nature?
questions.explanation: The nature element 'planned activities' emphasises that projects require careful planning before execution, ensuring that tasks, resources, and timelines are well-defined ahead of implementation.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes economic feasibility?
questions.explanation: Economic feasibility assesses financial viability by weighing projected costs against monetary benefits[cite: 3].

questions.stem: The nature element that describes a project as depending on human, financial, and material resources is:
questions.explanation: Resource dependent highlights that projects rely on human, financial, and material resources for execution - making resource planning and allocation a critical part of project management.

questions.stem: Summative evaluation focuses on:
questions.explanation: Summative evaluation takes place at the end to summarize overall results and long-term impacts[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A state government initiates a project to provide clean water to a rural community suffering from waterborne diseases. Which element of the nature of a project does this BEST illustrate?
questions.explanation: Projects initiated to address an identified need or problem reflect the problem-solving mechanism element of a project's nature - the rural water project directly responds to a health problem in the community.

questions.stem: What is the key benefit of the project life cycle?
questions.explanation: The life cycle provides a clear, structured framework to guide project work from start to finish[cite: 3].

questions.stem: How do projects primarily differ from daily organisational operations according to their nature?

options.A: Projects require more staff than routine operations
options.B: Projects are goal-oriented and time-bound, unlike daily operations
options.C: Projects are entirely funded by external bodies, unlike operations
options.D: Projects do not require any planning, unlike routine operations

questions.explanation: The lecture states that projects differ from daily organisational operations because they are goal-oriented and time-bound - they have a clear purpose and a defined end date, unlike continuous operational activities.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT correct about project management?

options.A: It has a beginning and an end
options.C: It outputs through the process of implementation

questions.explanation: Projects serve various entities including private corporations and non-profits, not exclusively the government[cite: 4].

questions.stem: The construction of a lecture hall that ends after completion best illustrates which project characteristic?
questions.explanation: The lecture uses construction of a lecture hall as the direct example of the 'definite beginning and end' characteristic - a project starts at a specific time and ends once its objectives are achieved.

questions.stem: Project management involves:
questions.explanation: Project management covers planning, execution, monitoring, and closing throughout the project lifecycle[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Establishment of a computer laboratory for students is given as an example of which project characteristic?
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly uses the establishment of a computer laboratory as an example of the 'specific objectives' characteristic - projects are undertaken to accomplish clearly defined goals.

questions.stem: Formula for ARR

options.C: Average income / Average rate of return

questions.explanation: Accounting Rate of Return (ARR) measures profitability from an accounting standpoint and is calculated as Average Income divided by Average Investment.

questions.stem: Two different organisations both construct science laboratories. Yet each project is considered distinct. Which characteristic accounts for this?
questions.explanation: Uniqueness states that each project produces a distinct outcome even when similar projects exist - context, stakeholders, location, and other factors make every project one-of-a-kind.

questions.stem: Effective utilization of resources is part of:
questions.explanation: The resource utilization criterion specifically examines how well inputs were managed[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project that runs beyond its scheduled completion date may experience increased costs or reduced effectiveness. This warning relates to which characteristic?
questions.explanation: The 'time bound' characteristic states that projects must be completed within a specified schedule and that delay may increase costs or reduce effectiveness - making deadline management a priority.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the monitoring and controlling phase?

options.B: To track performance and make adjustments

questions.explanation: Monitoring and controlling compares actual performance to plan and implements corrective actions[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Finance, manpower, materials, and equipment are all examples of which project characteristic?
questions.explanation: The 'limited resources' characteristic lists finance, manpower, materials, and equipment as the constraints within which projects must operate - reinforcing the need for efficient resource management.

questions.stem: If a project must be completed sooner, what is a likely trade-off?
questions.explanation: To compress time, you must either add resources (higher cost) or cut deliverable features (reduced scope)[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Price fluctuations, weather conditions, and technical failure are given as examples of:
questions.explanation: The lecture cites price fluctuations, weather conditions, and technical failure as examples of risk and uncertainty - unexpected events that may affect the success of a project.

questions.stem: Which phase consumes the most resources?
questions.explanation: Most time, money, and people are used during execution to perform the work[cite: 5].

questions.stem: Which characteristic highlights that project tasks depend on one another for successful completion?
questions.explanation: Interrelated activities is the characteristic that states project tasks are interdependent - the completion of one task often determines whether the next can begin, making sequencing and coordination essential.

questions.stem: Which phase involves documenting lessons learned?
questions.explanation: Lessons learned are captured at the end of the project during the closing phase[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A project that develops step-by-step from planning through to completion is demonstrating the characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Progressive development describes how projects advance incrementally - from initiation and planning through execution and monitoring to final closure - rather than being completed all at once.

questions.stem: What is a critical factor in Hackman’s Model for team effectiveness?
questions.explanation: Hackman's model highlights a clear, compelling direction as an essential condition for effectiveness[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which characteristic explains why projects usually involve collaboration among individuals with different skills?
questions.explanation: 'Requires teamwork' is the characteristic that acknowledges projects involve collaboration among people with varied skills - no single individual typically possesses all the expertise needed to deliver a complex project.

questions.stem: Which tool is commonly used for task scheduling in planning?
questions.explanation: Gantt charts are standard visual tools used to plan timelines and schedule dependent tasks[cite: 3].

questions.stem: How many major characteristics of a project are identified in the Week 2 lecture note?
questions.explanation: The Week 2 lecture identifies nine characteristics of a project: definite beginning and end, specific objectives, uniqueness, time bound, limited resources, interrelated activities, risk and uncertainty, requires teamwork, and progressive development.

questions.stem: What does technical feasibility assess?

options.A: Whether the project aligns with company goals
options.B: If the required technology and resources are available
options.D: The environmental impact of the project

questions.explanation: Technical feasibility evaluates software, hardware, infrastructure, and technical expertise availability[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which component of a project refers to the desired result to be achieved?
questions.explanation: Project objective is defined as the desired result to be achieved - it sets the direction and purpose of the entire project and guides all subsequent planning and execution activities.

questions.stem: Which of these is a typical attribute of project being analyzed in project portfolio management?
questions.explanation: Analyzing resource consumption across competing projects is a central attribute of portfolio management[cite: 4].

questions.stem: The work required to complete a project is described by which project component?
questions.explanation: Project scope defines the work required to complete the project - it establishes the boundaries of the project, clarifying what is and is not included in the deliverables.

questions.stem: Over-reliance on a single method can:
questions.explanation: Relying exclusively on one technique can distort evaluation results and create bias[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Individuals or groups interested in a project are referred to as:
questions.explanation: Stakeholders are defined as individuals or groups interested in the project - they may influence or be affected by project outcomes, and managing their expectations is a key project management responsibility.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a Belbin team role?
questions.explanation: Monitor Evaluator is one of Belbin’s official nine team roles[cite: 3].

questions.stem: The estimated cost of a project is captured in which component?
questions.explanation: Budget is the project component representing the estimated cost of executing the project - it guides financial planning and serves as the benchmark for controlling expenditure throughout the project lifecycle.

questions.stem: What does financial feasibility analyze?
questions.explanation: Financial feasibility evaluates capital requirements, expected cash flow, and return on investment[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Expected outputs of a project are known as:
questions.explanation: Deliverables are the expected outputs of a project - the tangible or intangible results that confirm project objectives have been met and that are handed over to the client or end-user upon completion.

questions.stem: Which of these is a key monitoring and controlling activity?
questions.explanation: Comparing actual performance metrics against baseline plans highlights variances for corrective action[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Human and material inputs required to execute a project are classified under which component?
questions.explanation: Resources refer to the human and material inputs needed for project execution - encompassing personnel, equipment, materials, and other assets required to carry out project activities.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a feasibility study?

options.B: To determine if the project is viable

questions.explanation: A feasibility study evaluates whether a proposed project is practically and financially viable[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A project plan states that a new school library will be built within 18 months. The 18-month period represents which project component?
questions.explanation: Project time frame is the component that defines the duration of project execution - in this case, the 18 months allocated for the construction of the school library.

questions.stem: Which planning technique helps identify potential delay risks?
questions.explanation: Proactive risk planning helps anticipate events that could delay the project schedule[cite: 3].

questions.stem: How many standard components of a project are identified in the Week 2 lecture?
questions.explanation: The Week 2 lecture identifies seven standard components of a project: project objective, project scope, project time frame, resources, budget, stakeholders, and deliverables.

questions.stem: What should be done after reporting findings?
questions.explanation: The ultimate goal of reporting evaluation findings is to implement necessary changes and improvements[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Building roads or classrooms is given as an example of which type of project?
questions.explanation: The lecture classifies building roads or classrooms under construction projects - physical infrastructure developments that have a tangible built output upon completion.

questions.stem: What is scope creep?
questions.explanation: Scope creep happens when new features or work are added without adjusting time or budget[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Rural electrification is an example of which type of project?
questions.explanation: Rural electrification is listed as an example of community development projects - initiatives aimed at improving the welfare and living standards of a community.

questions.stem: One of the final steps in evaluation is:
questions.explanation: After evaluation and analysis, actionable recommendations are generated for future action[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Curriculum development programmes are classified under which type of project?
questions.explanation: Curriculum development programmes are given as an example of educational projects - projects carried out within academic institutions to improve or redesign learning content and structures.

questions.stem: During which phase would you conduct a post-implementation review?
questions.explanation: Post-implementation reviews take place as part of the formal closing phase[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Opening a new business branch is an example of which type of project?
questions.explanation: Opening a new business branch is listed as an example of business projects - commercially motivated projects aimed at expanding an organisation's market presence or operational capacity.

questions.stem: Which constraint is primarily concerned with deadlines and schedules?
questions.explanation: The time constraint governs schedules, activity durations, and project deadlines[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A TASUED department organises a seminar on entrepreneurship for students. This activity is BEST classified as which type of project?
questions.explanation: The lecture lists departmental seminar organisation and ICT training programmes as examples of educational projects within the TASUED environment - making an entrepreneurship seminar an educational project.

questions.stem: What can lead to a narrow view in evaluation?
questions.explanation: Relying on only one method restricts perspective and can miss critical information[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a project from a routine operation?

options.A: A project is continuous while a routine operation is temporary
options.B: A project produces repetitive output while a routine operation produces unique output
options.C: A project is temporary with a unique output, while a routine operation is continuous with repetitive tasks
options.D: A project has no completion date while a routine operation ends after objectives are met

questions.explanation: The Week 2 comparison table clearly states that projects are temporary with unique outputs, whereas routine operations are continuous with repetitive tasks - the fundamental distinction between the two.

questions.stem: A project charter is created during:
questions.explanation: The project charter authorizes the project and is written in the initiation phase[cite: 5].

questions.stem: High uncertainty is associated with which type of organisational activity?
questions.explanation: The project vs routine operations comparison shows that projects are characterised by high uncertainty, while routine operations are predictable - reflecting the risks inherent in novel, one-time undertakings.

questions.stem: The critical path method (CPM) identifies:

options.A: The longest path of dependent tasks

questions.explanation: CPM pinpoints the longest sequence of dependent activities that dictates total project length[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A school's timetabling process happens every semester without any change in procedure. Compared to a project, this activity is best described as a:
questions.explanation: A recurring, unchanged timetabling process is a continuous, repetitive activity - a routine operation. It lacks the unique output, specific completion date, and high uncertainty that define a project.

questions.stem: When should stakeholder analysis be performed?
questions.explanation: Stakeholder dynamics change over time, requiring continuous analysis throughout the project[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which pair of attributes correctly describes a routine operation as distinguished from a project?
questions.explanation: Routine operations are characterised by continuity and repetition - they are ongoing activities with predictable outputs, unlike projects which are temporary and produce unique results.

questions.stem: What is a risk management plan used for?

options.B: To identify and mitigate potential risks

questions.explanation: A risk management plan anticipates uncertainties and establishes strategies to mitigate threats[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as an example of a project in the TASUED environment?

options.D: Routine security patrol of the campus

questions.explanation: The lecture specifically lists the students' entrepreneurship exhibition as an example of a project in the TASUED environment - alongside construction of lecture theatres, departmental seminars, ICT training, and research dissertations.

questions.stem: What triggers the Initiation phase?
questions.explanation: A business requirement, problem, or market opportunity initiates a project[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A student's research dissertation project at TASUED qualifies as a project because it:

options.A: Is carried out daily as part of normal academic work
options.B: Is a temporary, planned, unique activity with defined objectives and a completion date
options.C: Requires no resources and involves no risk
options.D: Is a continuous, repetitive departmental function

questions.explanation: A research dissertation is a temporary endeavour with clear objectives, a defined timeline, and a unique output - meeting all the characteristics that qualify it as a project in the TASUED environment.

questions.stem: A risk register documents:
questions.explanation: A risk register logs recognized risks, risk severity, and corresponding mitigation actions[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Understanding project characteristics helps project managers to do all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The lecture lists improving planning efficiency, allocating resources properly, controlling risks, ensuring timely completion, and enhancing success rate as benefits - but risk can only be controlled, not guaranteed to be zero.

questions.stem: The fundamental objective of Project Portfolio Management is to:

options.A: Framework and a defined way of doing things
options.B: Ensure that there is dynamic system within a larger organizational environment
options.C: Prioritize and assign resources to the right projects
options.D: Determine the optimal mix and sequencing of proposed projects to achieve overall goals

questions.explanation: Project Portfolio Management aims to determine the optimal mix and sequence of projects to maximize organizational goals[cite: 4].

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of benefits is correctly associated with understanding project characteristics?

options.A: Guarantee of full funding and elimination of all project delays
options.B: Improved planning efficiency and proper resource allocation
options.C: Reduction of team size and outsourcing of all project activities
options.D: Removal of stakeholder input and simplification of project scope

questions.explanation: The lecture states that understanding project characteristics helps improve planning efficiency and allocate resources properly - two of the five benefits listed for this knowledge.

questions.stem: If a project must be completed earlier than planned, what two constraints are most likely to be impacted?
questions.explanation: Shortening the timeline usually requires spending more money (crashing) or reducing deliverables (scope)[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a common problem in projects in the Week 2 lecture?

options.B: Poor supervision and lack of skilled manpower

questions.explanation: Poor supervision and lack of skilled manpower are both listed as common problems in projects - alongside poor definition of objectives, inadequate funding, and time mismanagement.

questions.stem: Which method involves checking availability and suitability of inputs?
questions.explanation: Resource checks ensure that necessary materials, inputs, and personnel are available[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project fails to achieve its goals because the team never clearly articulated what the project was supposed to accomplish. Which common project problem does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: When a project team does not clearly define what the project is meant to achieve, it reflects poor definition of objectives - a common project problem that leads to misdirected effort and eventual failure.

questions.stem: KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) are:
questions.explanation: KPIs are quantifiable measures used to track and evaluate performance success[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A construction project stalls three months before completion because funds run out. Which common problem does this represent?
questions.explanation: Running out of funds mid-project is a direct consequence of inadequate funding - listed as one of the common problems in projects that can halt execution and prevent goal achievement.

questions.stem: One of these is the consideration for chosen appropriate project management structure:
questions.explanation: Organizational context (culture, authority lines, environment) dictates the selection of project structure (e.g., matrix, functional)[cite: 4].

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists ALL seven components of a standard project?

options.A: Objective, scope, time frame, resources, budget, stakeholders, deliverables
options.B: Objective, scope, time frame, risk, budget, stakeholders, marketing plan
options.C: Planning, execution, monitoring, control, closing, review, approval
options.D: Objective, teamwork, uniqueness, risk, budget, timeline, report

questions.explanation: The seven standard project components listed in Week 2 are: project objective, project scope, project time frame, resources, budget, stakeholders, and deliverables - all seven are captured only in the first option.

questions.stem: Waterfall methodology is:
questions.explanation: Waterfall follows a sequential, phase-by-phase linear lifecycle structure[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project manager notices that Task B cannot begin until Task A is completed, and Task C depends on Task B. This interdependency reflects which project characteristic?
questions.explanation: The dependency chain (A → B → C) is a direct example of interrelated activities - the characteristic that states project tasks depend on one another for successful completion.

questions.stem: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) breaks down:
questions.explanation: A WBS decomposes major deliverables into smaller, manageable work components[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which combination of project characteristics most directly causes a project budget overrun when not properly managed?

options.B: Time bound, limited resources, and risk and uncertainty
options.D: Definite beginning and end, and interrelated activities

questions.explanation: Budget overruns are most directly caused by delays (time bound), resource constraints (limited resources), and unforeseen events (risk and uncertainty) - the three characteristics that place the greatest financial pressure on a project.

questions.stem: Risk management plans are developed in:
questions.explanation: Risks are identified, analyzed, and mitigation strategies are created during planning[cite: 5].

questions.stem: Using the Week 2 definition, which of the following activities qualifies as a project?

options.A: A bakery baking bread every morning
options.B: A hospital conducting daily patient check-ins
options.C: A community organisation building a new health clinic within 6 months
options.D: A security company providing 24-hour patrol services indefinitely

questions.explanation: Building a new health clinic within 6 months is a planned, temporary, goal-oriented, resource-dependent, and unique activity - matching the Week 2 definition. The other options are continuous, repetitive routine operations.

questions.stem: Initial cash outlay N500,000, inflows N50,000 for 15 years. Payback period?
questions.explanation: Payback Period = Initial Investment / Annual Cash Inflow = 500,000 / 50,000 = 10 years.

questions.stem: Which project component, if poorly defined, is MOST likely to cause a project team to work on activities outside the intended scope?
questions.explanation: Project scope defines the work required to complete the project. If poorly defined, team members may include unintended activities (scope creep) or miss critical ones - making clear scope definition fundamental to project control.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of team building activities?
questions.explanation: Team building strengthens interpersonal relationships, enhances trust, and improves communication[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A project to establish a new faculty at TASUED involves architects, lecturers, administrators, and government officials working together. Which characteristic of a project does this BEST demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The involvement of professionals from different fields - architects, lecturers, administrators, and government officials - directly demonstrates the 'requires teamwork' characteristic, which states projects involve collaboration among individuals with different skills.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of high-performing teams?
questions.explanation: High-performing teams require strong, open communication rather than poor communication[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which statement BEST summarises the core message of the Week 2 lecture on the meaning and characteristics of projects?

options.A: Projects are permanent organisational functions that require no planning
options.B: A project is a temporary, goal-oriented, and resource-constrained activity with identifiable characteristics that distinguish it from routine operations
options.C: Routine operations and projects are identical in nature, scope, and purpose
options.D: Projects succeed only when they are funded by external organisations

questions.explanation: The Week 2 summary states that a project is a temporary, goal-oriented activity undertaken to achieve specific results within limited time and resources, and that knowledge of project characteristics helps managers execute projects effectively - making this the most comprehensive summary.

questions.stem: Which technique helps prevent scope creep?
questions.explanation: A formal change control process ensures proposed changes are thoroughly evaluated before approval[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an example of a project stakeholder in the Week 3 lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture lists project sponsor, project manager, team members, customers, government agencies, and community members as stakeholder examples. Competitors are not mentioned as project stakeholders.

questions.stem: How can leaders foster adaptability in teams?
questions.explanation: Encouraging psychological safety, continuous learning, and flexiblity helps teams adapt[cite: 3].

questions.stem: According to the Week 3 lecture, project management is best defined as:

options.A: The informal coordination of staff to meet daily organisational targets
options.B: The systematic process of applying knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities to achieve specific goals within defined constraints
options.C: The financial auditing of project expenditures at the end of every fiscal year
options.D: The recruitment and deployment of skilled workers for permanent organisational roles

questions.explanation: Week 3 defines project management as the systematic process of applying knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities in order to achieve specific goals within defined constraints such as time, cost, and quality.

questions.stem: Project evaluation helps in:
questions.explanation: Evaluations provide evidence-based insights for making informed decisions[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Project management ensures the coordination of resources and activities toward:

options.D: Reduction of the project team size

questions.explanation: The lecture states that project management ensures coordination of resources and activities toward successful project completion - the overarching aim of all project management efforts.

questions.stem: ARR has an advantage over the payback period because

options.B: It ignores time value of money

questions.explanation: ARR evaluates overall profitability by accounting for income/profit after tax throughout the project's entire lifespan, unlike payback which only focuses on liquidity and cash recovery time.

questions.stem: A project goal is best described as:

options.A: A specific, measurable target set for each team member
options.B: The overall purpose or final achievement expected from a project
options.C: The detailed schedule of project activities and deadlines
options.D: The total cost estimate for completing the project

questions.explanation: A project goal is defined as the overall purpose or final achievement expected from a project - it is the broad desired end-state that the project is designed to reach, distinct from the specific measurable objectives.

questions.stem: Why is understanding team development models important for project managers?

options.C: It aids in guiding team dynamics and productivity
options.D: It eliminates the need for communication

questions.explanation: Knowing team development models enables managers to resolve friction and support team productivity[cite: 3].

questions.stem: 'Improving students' access to ICT facilities' is given as an example of a:
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly uses 'improving students' access to ICT facilities' as an example of a project goal - the overall purpose or final achievement expected from the project.

questions.stem: What does inconsistent data collection affect?
questions.explanation: Inconsistent collection methods compromise data quality and lower the reliability of findings[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Project objectives differ from project goals in that objectives are:

options.A: Broad, general aspirations for the entire project
options.B: Specific and measurable targets that guide project implementation
options.C: Unlimited in scope and not bound by any timeline
options.D: Restricted to the financial aspects of the project only

questions.explanation: While a project goal is the overall purpose, objectives are specific and measurable targets that guide project implementation - breaking the goal down into actionable, trackable steps.

questions.stem: Which document is created during the initiation phase to formally authorize a project?
questions.explanation: The project charter gives authority to proceed with the project[cite: 3].

questions.stem: The acronym SMART, used to describe good project objectives, stands for:
questions.explanation: The lecture lists the characteristics of good objectives as Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, and Time-bound - forming the SMART criteria widely used in project and performance management.

questions.stem: How does scope creep affect projects?

options.B: It leads to uncontrolled expansion of deliverables

questions.explanation: Scope creep causes unapproved expansion of deliverables, threatening budget and schedule[cite: 3].

questions.stem: 'Train as many staff members as possible in data analysis sometime next year' - which SMART criteria does this objective FAIL to meet?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'as many as possible' is not a specific or measurable target, and 'sometime next year' is not a defined deadline - failing three SMART criteria simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which activity is part of monitoring and controlling?
questions.explanation: Measuring performance metrics allows project teams to monitor budget variance and schedule progress[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the SMART characteristics of a good project objective?
questions.explanation: The SMART criteria listed in the lecture are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, and Time-bound. 'Affordable' is not among them - budget considerations fall under the project constraint of cost, not the SMART framework.

questions.stem: Which practice helps teams transition from Storming to Norming?

options.B: Establishing clear norms and conflict-resolution processes

questions.explanation: Setting ground rules and formal conflict-resolution workflows guides teams past storming[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Project scope is defined as:

options.A: The estimated budget allocated to a project
options.B: The total work required to complete a project successfully
options.C: The list of team members assigned to a project
options.D: The timeline showing project start and end dates

questions.explanation: Project scope refers to the total work required to complete a project successfully - it defines what is included, what is excluded, and the boundaries of the project.

questions.stem: WBS stands for
questions.explanation: WBS stands for Work Breakdown Structure, which is a key deliverable-oriented breakdown of a project into smaller components.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of what project scope defines?

options.A: What is included in the project
options.B: What is excluded from the project
options.D: The personal goals of the project manager

questions.explanation: Project scope defines what is included, what is excluded, and the project boundaries - it is focused on the work of the project, not the personal ambitions of the project manager.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a common cause of project delays?
questions.explanation: Having a clear, well-defined scope prevents delays rather than causing them[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A project team begins adding tasks that were not part of the original plan, causing cost and time overruns. This problem is most directly caused by a poorly defined:
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled addition of tasks beyond the original plan - commonly called scope creep - is the direct result of a poorly defined project scope, which should specify exactly what is and is not included in the project.

questions.stem: Stakeholder approval is typically secured in which phase?
questions.explanation: Stakeholder sign-off is needed to start the project formally[cite: 5].

questions.stem: Stakeholders in a project are defined as:

options.A: Only the financial sponsors who fund the project
options.B: Individuals or groups who have interest in or are affected by a project
options.C: The technical experts responsible for project execution only
options.D: Government agencies that regulate project activities

questions.explanation: Stakeholders are defined as individuals or groups who have interest in or are affected by a project - a broad category that includes the project sponsor, manager, team members, customers, government agencies, and community members.

questions.stem: External evaluation is performed by:
questions.explanation: External evaluation utilizes outside, independent third parties for objectivity[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A local government, the construction company, nearby residents, and the funding bank are all involved in a road project. Collectively, they are referred to as:
questions.explanation: All parties who have interest in or are affected by the road project - the local government, construction company, residents, and bank - are collectively referred to as stakeholders.

questions.stem: Who approves the project charter?
questions.explanation: Project sponsors or key decision-making stakeholders sign off on and approve the charter[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Deliverables in project management are best described as:

options.A: Significant points used to measure project progress
options.B: Measurable outputs or results produced at the completion of a project or project phase
options.C: The schedule of activities showing start and end dates
options.D: Resources assigned to the project team for execution

questions.explanation: Deliverables are defined as measurable outputs or results produced at the completion of a project or project phase - they are the tangible or verifiable outcomes that signal project progress or completion.

questions.stem: What is a key advantage of the project life cycle?

options.B: Provides a structured framework for management

questions.explanation: The life cycle offers a organized structure for project oversight[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A completed building, a training report, and a software product are all examples of:
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly lists a completed building, a training report, and a software product as examples of deliverables - the measurable outputs produced at the completion of a project or phase.

questions.stem: Who typically conducts the feasibility study?
questions.explanation: Feasibility studies are best performed by an independent or objective team to ensure unbiased analysis[cite: 3].

questions.stem: What is the key difference between a deliverable and a milestone?

options.A: A deliverable is a significant stage in the project, while a milestone is a measurable output
options.B: A deliverable is a measurable output produced at project completion, while a milestone is a significant point used to measure progress
options.C: A deliverable refers to financial resources, while a milestone refers to human resources
options.D: A deliverable is set at the start of a project, while a milestone is set at the end

questions.explanation: Deliverables are measurable outputs or results produced at completion, while milestones are significant points or stages used to measure performance - they serve different purposes in tracking project progress.

questions.stem: Which technique helps manage the triple constraints effectively?
questions.explanation: A formal change control process evaluates trade-off impacts on time, scope, and budget[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Milestones in project management are defined as:

options.A: The total budget allocated for each project phase
options.B: Significant points or stages in project progress used to measure performance
options.C: The list of all resources required to complete a project
options.D: Written records relating to all project activities

questions.explanation: Milestones are defined as significant points or stages in project progress used to measure performance - they act as checkpoints that confirm the project is advancing as planned.

questions.stem: What is the benefit of documenting lessons learned?

options.D: To replace the need for planning

questions.explanation: Lessons learned provide valuable organizational knowledge to improve performance in future projects[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Completion of foundation work and approval of project design are given as examples of:
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly uses completion of foundation work and approval of project design as examples of milestones - significant points in the project lifecycle used to gauge whether the project is on track.

questions.stem: What is the most likely consequence of inadequate project planning?
questions.explanation: Poor planning causes unexpected obstacles, bottlenecks, and timeline delays[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A project manager sets a checkpoint to confirm that structural drawings have been approved before construction begins. This checkpoint is an example of a:
questions.explanation: A checkpoint marking the approval of structural drawings before construction proceeds is a milestone - a significant stage in project progress used to confirm that prerequisites have been met before moving forward.

questions.stem: Benchmarking compares project performance against:
questions.explanation: Benchmarking measures outcomes against external industry standards or past benchmarks[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project schedule is defined as a document that:

options.A: Lists all individuals and organisations interested in the project
options.B: Shows timelines for completion of project activities, including start date, end date, and sequence
options.C: Estimates the total financial cost of executing the project
options.D: Identifies potential risks that may affect the project

questions.explanation: A project schedule shows timelines for completion of project activities, indicating the start date, end date, and sequence of activities - providing the time-based roadmap for project execution.

questions.stem: What improves stakeholder buy-in?
questions.explanation: Active stakeholder engagement builds trust, alignment, and commitment[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT indicated by a project schedule?
questions.explanation: A project schedule indicates start dates, end dates, and the sequence of activities. The names of stakeholders are captured in a stakeholder register, not the project schedule.

questions.stem: Which model describes team development in the sequence of Forming, Storming, Norming, Performing?
questions.explanation: Tuckman's model outlines the stage sequence of team growth[cite: 3].

questions.stem: In project management, resources are best described as:

options.A: Significant progress checkpoints within the project
options.B: Written records relating to project activities
options.C: Inputs required to execute a project
options.D: Uncertain events that may affect project outcomes

questions.explanation: Resources are defined as inputs required to execute a project - encompassing human resources, financial resources, materials, equipment, and technology.

questions.stem: In which phase is the feasibility study usually conducted?
questions.explanation: Feasibility studies are carried out early in the initiation phase to validate project viability[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a type of project resource in the Week 3 lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture lists human resources, financial resources, materials, equipment, and technology as types of project resources. Stakeholder opinions are part of project communication, not a resource type.

questions.stem: What is the first step in project evaluation?
questions.explanation: Evaluation starts with clearly stating its goals so every other step is focused and purposeful[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project requires engineers, construction materials, excavators, and a budget of ₦50 million. All these items are collectively referred to as:
questions.explanation: Engineers (human resources), construction materials, excavators (equipment), and the budget (financial resources) are all types of project resources - the inputs required to execute the project.

questions.stem: What is the best way to mitigate delays caused by material shortages?
questions.explanation: Advance purchasing and supply chain planning mitigate lead-time material delays[cite: 3].

questions.stem: How many methods of project selection are identified in the Week 6 lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies four methods of project selection: cost-benefit analysis, feasibility study, expert judgment, and scoring model.

questions.stem: What is the final outcome of a feasibility study?
questions.explanation: A feasibility study produces a formal recommendation leading to a Go or No-Go decision[cite: 3].

questions.stem: The three major constraints within which every project operates are collectively known as:
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies the three major project constraints - time, cost, and scope/quality - as the Triple Constraint, a fundamental concept in project management.

questions.stem: Why is the iron triangle important in project management?

options.B: It provides a framework for trade-off decisions
options.D: It replaces the need for planning

questions.explanation: It helps managers analyze the consequences and make trade-offs when project variables change[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists the three elements of the Triple Constraint?
questions.explanation: The Triple Constraint consists of time, cost, and scope/quality - the three interdependent constraints that every project must balance. A change in one directly affects the other two.

questions.stem: Which is NOT a phase of project evaluation?
questions.explanation: Employee training is an implementation or HR activity, not a phase in evaluation[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project sponsor instructs the team to expand the project scope without increasing the budget. Based on the Triple Constraint, this decision will most likely affect:

options.B: The project time frame, since more work with the same budget typically takes longer
options.D: The project goal, which will need to be redefined

questions.explanation: The Triple Constraint states that a change in one constraint affects the others. Expanding scope without increasing cost means more work must be done with the same resources, which typically extends the time needed to complete the project.

questions.stem: In Drexler-Sibbet’s team performance model, which stage involves building trust and personal connection?
questions.explanation: Trust Building is Stage 2 of the Drexler-Sibbet model, establishing mutual respect and relationships[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which statement about project constraints is TRUE according to the Week 3 lecture?

options.A: The three constraints operate independently and changes in one have no effect on others
options.B: Only cost is a binding constraint; time and scope can be adjusted freely
options.C: A change in one constraint affects the other constraints
options.D: Project constraints apply only during the planning phase

questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly states that a change in one of the Triple Constraints affects the others - making constraint management one of the most critical balancing acts in project management.

questions.stem: Which is not one of the reasons why we need project portfolio management (PPM) system?
questions.explanation: While Project Portfolio Management (PPM) improves strategic alignment and resource allocation, it cannot completely guarantee the success of every project.

questions.stem: In project management, risk is defined as:

options.A: The total cost overrun at the end of a project
options.B: Uncertain events that may positively or negatively affect project objectives
options.C: The planned budget reserved for project execution
options.D: The formal process of closing a completed project

questions.explanation: Risk is defined as uncertain events that may positively or negatively affect project objectives - acknowledging that not all risks are threats; some may create opportunities that benefit the project.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between quality and the triple constraints?

options.B: Quality is unaffected by scope, cost, or time
options.C: Quality depends on balancing scope, cost, and time
options.D: Quality replaces scope in the iron triangle
