questions.explanation: Quality sits in the center of the triangle and depends on properly balancing scope, cost, and time[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Financial shortage, equipment failure, and weather conditions are given as examples of:
questions.explanation: The lecture lists financial shortage, equipment failure, and weather conditions as examples of project risks - uncertain events that could negatively affect the project's objectives, timeline, or budget.

questions.stem: One of these is not a component of Techno-Economic Feasibility Studies
questions.explanation: Market penetration is a marketing strategy concept, whereas project background, demand studies, and demand projections are core components of a Techno-Economic Feasibility Study.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST reflects the Week 3 understanding of project risk?

options.A: Risks only have negative effects and should always be avoided
options.B: Risks are certain events that occur at every stage of the project
options.C: Risks are uncertain events that may have positive or negative effects on a project
options.D: Risks are only financial in nature and relate to budget shortfalls

questions.explanation: The lecture's definition of risk emphasises uncertainty and acknowledges both positive and negative impacts - a risk could be a threat (e.g. equipment failure) or an opportunity (e.g. a cost reduction due to favourable exchange rates).

questions.stem: What does quality of deliverables evaluate?
questions.explanation: Quality of deliverables assesses if outputs meet predefined criteria and standards[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists the five project management processes in their proper sequence?

options.A: Planning → Initiation → Execution → Closure → Monitoring and Control
options.B: Initiation → Planning → Execution → Monitoring and Control → Closure
options.C: Execution → Planning → Initiation → Monitoring and Control → Closure
options.D: Initiation → Execution → Planning → Closure → Monitoring and Control

questions.explanation: The five project management processes listed in Week 3 follow this sequence: Initiation (defining the project), Planning (developing strategies), Execution (implementing plans), Monitoring and Control (tracking progress), and Closure (completing the project).

questions.stem: Which activity occurs in the Closing phase?

options.D: Starting a new project without review

questions.explanation: Capturing lessons learned is a standard closeout activity[cite: 3].

questions.stem: The process of defining a project is associated with which project management process?
questions.explanation: Initiation is the process group focused on defining the project - establishing its purpose, objectives, and feasibility before planning and execution begin.

questions.stem: The term "crashing" in project management means:

options.A: Reducing project duration at higher cost

questions.explanation: Crashing compresses schedule duration by adding extra resources, which increases total cost[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Tracking the progress of a project and taking corrective action falls under which process?
questions.explanation: Monitoring and Control involves tracking project progress and taking corrective actions to keep the project aligned with its plan - ensuring performance stays within approved time, cost, and scope baselines.

questions.stem: Which symptom indicates a team is in the "Storming" stage?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal disagreements and power struggles over authority define the Storming phase[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Developing strategies for a project is the primary focus of which process group?
questions.explanation: Planning is the process group focused on developing strategies - it produces the roadmap for how the project will be executed, monitored, and closed.

questions.stem: SCBA and CCBA differ mainly in:
questions.explanation: CCBA relies strictly on market price valuations, while SCBA uses shadow pricing and broader metrics[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project has been delivered, accepted by the client, and all documentation has been filed. This represents which project management process?
questions.explanation: Closure is the final process group, which involves completing the project, obtaining formal acceptance, archiving documentation, and releasing the project team - all of which are described in this scenario.

questions.stem: An evaluation report should include:
questions.explanation: Evaluation reports document key findings, recommendations, and next action steps[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project team is defined as:

options.A: Only the project manager and the project sponsor
options.B: Individuals assigned different responsibilities for project execution
options.C: External consultants hired to audit project expenditures
options.D: The government body responsible for approving project activities

questions.explanation: A project team consists of individuals assigned different responsibilities for project execution - including the project manager, engineers/experts, account officers, supervisors, and support staff.

questions.stem: The following are internal constraints for project delays EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Law and order problems are external political/environmental constraints, whereas incompetency, skill gaps, and technological bottlenecks are internal constraints[cite: 4].

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a member of a project team in the Week 3 lecture?
questions.explanation: The project team members listed in the lecture are the project manager, engineers/experts, account officers, supervisors, and support staff. External media consultants are not included.

questions.stem: What is the role of a project sponsor?

options.A: To do all the project work

questions.explanation: Project sponsors champion the project, secure executive buy-in, and provide financial resources and support[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A project sponsor is best described as:

options.A: A team member responsible for day-to-day project supervision
options.B: The individual or organisation that provides financial and managerial support for the project
options.C: A government regulator who approves project activities
options.D: An external auditor who reviews project expenditures

questions.explanation: A project sponsor is defined as the individual or organisation that provides financial and managerial support for the project - responsible for funding approval, policy direction, and performance oversight.

questions.stem: Which model focuses on five dysfunctions of a team: absence of trust, fear of conflict, etc.?
questions.explanation: Patrick Lencioni's model addresses the Five Dysfunctions of a Team[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is a responsibility of the project sponsor?

options.A: Writing daily progress reports for team members
options.B: Conducting site inspections on behalf of the project manager
options.D: Designing the project schedule and assigning tasks

questions.explanation: The lecture lists funding approval, policy direction, and performance oversight as the responsibilities of the project sponsor - distinguishing this strategic support role from the operational role of the project manager.

questions.stem: What is used to compare social costs and benefits?
questions.explanation: Social Cost-Benefit Analysis (SCBA) weighs non-market social impacts and expenditures[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Project communication involves:

options.A: Allocating financial resources to project activities
options.D: Setting project milestones for each phase

questions.explanation: Project communication is defined as sharing project information among stakeholders - ensuring all parties are kept informed about project status, decisions, and changes.

questions.stem: What is the primary goal of the planning phase?
questions.explanation: Planning involves setting up the scope, schedule, and resources through detailed project plans[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Effective project communication ensures all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The lecture states that effective project communication ensures coordination, problem solving, decision making, and transparency. Communication can help manage risks but cannot eliminate all of them.

questions.stem: Efficient resource allocation is a:
questions.explanation: Evaluation helps optimize and ensure efficient allocation of resources[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project team that frequently misses deadlines because members are unaware of each other's tasks is experiencing a failure in:
questions.explanation: Unawareness of teammates' tasks and resulting missed deadlines are symptoms of poor project communication - a breakdown in the sharing of project information among stakeholders that undermines coordination.

questions.stem: How can time constraints be managed effectively?
questions.explanation: When time is constrained, managers can re-balance by reducing scope or increasing budget[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Project documentation refers to:

options.A: The physical materials and equipment used during project execution
options.B: Written records relating to project activities
options.C: The informal verbal agreements made between team members
options.D: The financial investments provided by the project sponsor

questions.explanation: Project documentation is defined as written records relating to project activities - providing a formal, auditable trail of decisions, progress, and outcomes throughout the project lifecycle.

questions.stem: What is the major benefit of conducting a feasibility study?

options.B: Identifying potential problems and assessing viability

questions.explanation: The primary benefit of a feasibility study is to discover critical risks, identify potential obstacles, and confirm overall project viability before major capital is committed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an example of project documentation in the Week 3 lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture lists the project proposal, budget reports, progress reports, and final report as examples of project documentation. Stakeholder résumés are personal documents and are not classified as project documentation.

questions.stem: Which type of analysis considers pollution?
questions.explanation: SCBA measures environmental externalities like pollution[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project manager compiles written records of expenditures, work completed, and challenges encountered during a project. This activity relates to which project management concept?
questions.explanation: Compiling written records of expenditures, completed work, and challenges falls under project documentation - the systematic maintenance of written records relating to project activities.

questions.stem: In which Tuckman stage do teams begin to work more cohesively and establish norms?
questions.explanation: Cohesion and mutual trust develop as rules and norms are set in the Norming stage[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Understanding project terminologies helps project managers to do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.C: Guarantee that no project will ever fail

questions.explanation: The lecture states that understanding terminologies helps improve professional communication, enhance planning accuracy, reduce misunderstandings, facilitate effective monitoring, and promote successful delivery - but it cannot guarantee zero project failures.

questions.stem: Which step follows analyzing data?
questions.explanation: After data analysis is complete, the evaluation proceeds to assessing project performance[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which benefit of understanding project terminologies relates to preventing confusion arising from the use of unfamiliar terms?
questions.explanation: Reducing misunderstandings is the benefit of understanding project terminologies that directly addresses confusion caused by unfamiliar or misinterpreted terms - ensuring all team members share a common language.

questions.stem: Which model describes the stages of team development as Forming, Storming, Norming, and Performing?
questions.explanation: Bruce Tuckman established the classic 4-stage model of team development[cite: 3].

questions.stem: How many steps in the project evaluation process are outlined in the lecture note?
questions.explanation: The lecture outlines five steps in the project evaluation process: define evaluation objectives, identify evaluation criteria, collect relevant data, analyse the data, and draw conclusions and make recommendations.

questions.stem: Which factor is NOT typically analyzed during a feasibility study?
questions.explanation: Team performance evaluations take place during project execution or post-project reviews[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a common error arising from poor understanding of project management concepts?
questions.explanation: Budget overrun is listed as one of the common errors that result from poor understanding of project management concepts - alongside undefined project scope, miscommunication, time delays, and poor coordination.

questions.stem: The Planning phase includes:
questions.explanation: Planning includes breaking down tasks (WBS), estimating time, and setting schedules[cite: 5].

questions.stem: A project team operates without a clearly defined scope, leading to uncontrolled additions of work. This error falls under which common problem caused by poor concept understanding?
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled additions of work (scope creep) are directly caused by an undefined project scope - a common error resulting from poor understanding of the scope concept, which should set clear boundaries for project work.

questions.stem: What is the main focus of quality control activities?
questions.explanation: Quality control verifies that specific deliverable outputs meet defined technical specifications[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which pair of common errors from poor concept understanding are most closely related to each other?

options.B: Miscommunication among team members and poor coordination
options.C: Undefined project scope and efficient resource utilisation

questions.explanation: Miscommunication and poor coordination are directly linked - when team members fail to share information effectively, coordination breaks down, causing activities to clash, overlap, or be missed entirely.

questions.stem: Project evaluation contributes most to:
questions.explanation: Evaluation supports continuous organizational learning and procedural growth[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A university wants to establish a new digital library. The university's IT department, librarians, students, the construction company, and the funding bank are all involved. Which project management concept best describes this group collectively?
questions.explanation: All parties with an interest in or affected by the digital library project - the IT department, librarians, students, construction company, and funding bank - are collectively referred to as stakeholders.

questions.stem: Which constraint is NOT part of the "Iron Triangle"?
questions.explanation: The Iron Triangle parameters consist only of scope, cost, and time[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which combination of project management concepts would a manager use to answer the questions: 'What must be done?' 'By when?' 'With what?' and 'At what cost?'

options.B: Project scope, project schedule, resources, and budget
options.C: Project goal, project team, documentation, and communication

questions.explanation: Project scope answers 'What must be done?'; project schedule answers 'By when?'; resources answer 'With what?'; and budget answers 'At what cost?' - these four concepts together define the operational framework of a project.

questions.stem: The relationship between a sample variance whose variance is 2.01 and 0.44 is given as:
questions.explanation: The sum of activity variances along the path ($2.01 + 0.44 = 2.45$) determines total network variance[cite: 4].

questions.stem: During a hospital construction project, the team discovers that steel prices have risen sharply, threatening the budget. This situation is best described as a:
questions.explanation: A sudden rise in steel prices is an uncertain event that negatively affects the project's budget - a direct example of a project risk (specifically, financial shortage due to price fluctuation), as listed in the lecture.

questions.stem: The purpose of a feasibility study is to:
questions.explanation: A feasibility study evaluates practical, technical, and financial viability prior to starting a project[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project manager is reviewing a document that lists task names, assigned team members, start dates, and completion dates. This document is BEST described as a:
questions.explanation: A document listing task names, assigned members, start dates, and completion dates is a project schedule - it shows timelines for project activities and the sequence in which they are to be completed.

questions.stem: A benefit of project evaluation is:
questions.explanation: Evaluation helps organizations learn from past performance to improve future projects[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following scenarios demonstrates the concept of a project milestone?

options.A: A team submits its final project report to the client
options.B: A project receives additional funding from a new sponsor
options.C: The structural frame of a building is approved and signed off before roofing begins
options.D: A team member resigns from the project midway through execution

questions.explanation: Approval of a structural frame before the next phase of construction begins is a classic milestone - a significant point in project progress used to confirm readiness to move forward, consistent with the lecture's examples.

questions.stem: Closure involves:

options.A: Final deliverables, lessons learned, and handoffs

questions.explanation: The final phase includes handing over results, analyzing outcomes, and closing contracts[cite: 5].

questions.stem: Which project management concept serves as a 'common language' that allows project managers and team members to communicate professionally and without ambiguity?
questions.explanation: The lecture concludes that project management terminology provides a common language for managing projects effectively - enabling professional communication, reducing misunderstandings, and facilitating efficient project delivery.

questions.stem: Which comes after assessing performance?
questions.explanation: Once performance is assessed, evaluators identify specific strengths and weaknesses[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Project classification is best defined as:

options.A: The process of assigning team members to specific project tasks
options.B: The grouping of projects based on their purpose, size, ownership, complexity, or area of application
options.C: The scheduling of project activities from initiation to closure
options.D: The identification of risks associated with different project phases

questions.explanation: Project classification is defined in Week 4 as the grouping of projects based on their purpose, size, ownership, complexity, or area of application - enabling project managers to apply suitable planning and management approaches.

questions.stem: What is the main output of the Planning phase?
questions.explanation: The detailed project management plan is the comprehensive output of planning[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a basis for differentiating project types in the Week 4 lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture states that projects may differ in objectives, duration, cost implication, level of risk, and required expertise. Team member nationality is not a basis for project classification.

questions.stem: Which one is a proactive step in evaluation?
questions.explanation: Evaluating before project implementation is a proactive step to prevent failure[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Understanding project classification helps project managers to:

options.A: Eliminate all risks associated with the project
options.B: Apply appropriate planning methods, management techniques, and evaluation procedures
options.C: Guarantee project completion within the original budget
options.D: Avoid the need for stakeholder communication

questions.explanation: The introduction states that understanding project types helps managers apply appropriate planning methods, management techniques, and evaluation procedures - tailoring their approach to the specific nature of the project.

questions.stem: Traditional method of evaluating project include all except
questions.explanation: Gantt Chart is a visual tool used for project scheduling and planning, whereas IRR, ARR, and Payback Period are methods used for financial evaluation of projects.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes construction projects?

options.A: Projects focused on generating new knowledge through systematic investigation
options.B: Projects that involve physical development or infrastructural works
options.C: Projects aimed at improving the welfare of a community or society
options.D: Projects involving the development or installation of technological systems

questions.explanation: Construction projects are defined as those involving physical development or infrastructural works - encompassing school buildings, roads, bridges, housing projects, and office complexes.

questions.stem: Quantitative evaluation uses:
questions.explanation: Quantitative methods analyze measurable numerical metrics like budget variations[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of construction projects?

options.A: Short duration and low capital requirement
options.C: Capital intensive with high risk involvement
options.D: Focuses primarily on social welfare improvement

questions.explanation: Construction projects are characterised as capital intensive, long in duration, requiring technical expertise, and involving high risk - distinguishing them from other project types.

questions.stem: What is a common cause of "team falls" (team failures)?
questions.explanation: Ambiguous, poorly defined goals are a leading cause of project team failure[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Road construction, bridges, and housing projects are examples of which type of project?
questions.explanation: Road construction, bridges, and housing projects are all explicitly listed as examples of construction projects - physical development initiatives that create tangible built infrastructure.

questions.stem: What is a critical output of the planning phase?
questions.explanation: The comprehensive project management plan is the main output of the planning phase[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A construction project requires specialised engineers, architects, and surveyors. Which characteristic of construction projects does this reflect?
questions.explanation: The need for specialised professionals such as engineers, architects, and surveyors reflects the 'requires technical expertise' characteristic of construction projects listed in the Week 4 lecture.

questions.stem: Which of the following involves documenting and communicating results?
questions.explanation: Reporting findings is about presenting and sharing the outcomes with key stakeholders[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Business or commercial projects are primarily aimed at:

options.A: Generating new knowledge through academic research
options.B: Improving the physical infrastructure of a community
options.D: Addressing social challenges and promoting societal well-being

questions.explanation: Business or commercial projects aim at profit generation or business expansion - with objectives of increasing profitability, improving market share, and enhancing productivity.

questions.stem: What is the primary focus of Hackman's Team Effectiveness Model?
questions.explanation: Hackman's model stresses organizational support systems, structural design, and group coaching[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as an example of a business or commercial project?
questions.explanation: A market expansion programme is explicitly listed as an example of a business or commercial project - alongside establishment of a new business, product development, and opening new company branches.

questions.stem: Process evaluation focuses on:
questions.explanation: Process evaluation checks how operational activities were executed[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Increasing profitability, improving market share, and enhancing productivity are objectives associated with which type of project?
questions.explanation: Increasing profitability, improving market share, and enhancing productivity are the stated objectives of business or commercial projects - reflecting their commercial and profit-driven nature.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a kickoff meeting?
questions.explanation: A kickoff meeting brings stakeholders and team members together to formally start execution[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Educational projects are undertaken to:

options.B: Improve teaching, learning, and academic development
options.D: Develop new technological systems for organisations

questions.explanation: Educational projects are specifically defined as those undertaken to improve teaching, learning, and academic development - covering curriculum development, school renovation, student programmes, and academic events.

questions.stem: What is a critical success factor across all project phases?
questions.explanation: Having specific, measurable objectives provides alignment across every project phase[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Academic conferences, workshops, and curriculum development are examples of which type of project?
questions.explanation: Academic conferences, workshops, and curriculum development are all listed as examples of educational projects - activities designed to improve the academic environment and learning outcomes.

questions.stem: Which phase of the project life cycle involves defining the project at a high level and securing approval?
questions.explanation: The initiation phase focuses on defining the high-level business objective and obtaining approval to begin[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A state government funds the renovation of 50 public primary schools to improve learning conditions. This initiative is BEST classified as:

options.B: A government/public sector project and an educational project

questions.explanation: The initiative is funded by government (making it a public sector project) and is designed to improve learning conditions (making it an educational project) - demonstrating that a single project can span multiple classification categories.

questions.stem: If a project's scope increases while time and cost remain fixed, what typically happens to quality?
questions.explanation: Stretching resources to cover more scope without extra time or money compromises quality[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Research projects are primarily focused on:

options.B: Generating new knowledge or solving identified problems through systematic investigation
options.C: Expanding market share and increasing profitability
options.D: Installing technological systems for organisational use

questions.explanation: Research projects are defined as those focused on generating new knowledge or solving identified problems through systematic investigation - characterised by data collection, hypothesis testing, and evidence-based conclusions.

questions.stem: What is the most effective way to handle unavoidable delays?

options.B: Update the schedule and communicate changes

questions.explanation: When delays are inevitable, adjust schedule baselines and notify all stakeholders promptly[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of research projects?

options.A: Capital intensive with long implementation period
options.B: High risk and technical expertise in construction
options.C: Data collection, hypothesis testing, and evidence-based conclusions
options.D: Focus on profit generation and market expansion

questions.explanation: The lecture identifies data collection and analysis, hypothesis testing, and evidence-based conclusions as the defining features of research projects - reflecting their systematic, investigative nature.

questions.stem: Scope creep refers to:
questions.explanation: Scope creep occurs when project requirements expand without formal control or approval[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Undergraduate research projects, postgraduate dissertations, and scientific experiments are examples of:
questions.explanation: Undergraduate research projects, postgraduate dissertations, and scientific experiments are all explicitly listed as examples of research projects - systematic investigations aimed at generating new knowledge.

questions.stem: Which feasibility dimension considers organizational culture and user acceptance?
questions.explanation: Operational feasibility checks if end users will accept the solution and fit it into corporate workflows[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Community development projects are aimed at:

options.B: Improving the welfare of a community or society
options.C: Creating new knowledge through academic research

questions.explanation: Community development projects are defined as those aimed at improving the welfare of a community or society - encompassing rural electrification, borehole water projects, health campaigns, and environmental sanitation programmes.

questions.stem: A key feature of CCBA is:
questions.explanation: CCBA focuses on commercial outcomes, business returns, and firm reputation[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Rural electrification, borehole water projects, and environmental sanitation programmes are examples of:
questions.explanation: Rural electrification, borehole water projects, and environmental sanitation programmes are all listed as examples of community development projects - initiatives that directly improve the welfare and living standards of a community.

questions.stem: A Gantt chart visualizes:
questions.explanation: Gantt charts illustrate project schedules using timeline bar charts[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A non-governmental organisation launches a health awareness campaign in rural villages. This is BEST classified as a:
questions.explanation: A health awareness campaign targeting rural communities is a community development project - an initiative aimed at improving the welfare of a community, consistent with the examples given in the lecture.

questions.stem: What is the primary goal of the "Performing" stage?

options.B: To achieve high efficiency and results

questions.explanation: The primary focus in Performing is producing high output efficiently to hit project objectives[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Information Technology (IT) projects are defined as projects involving:

options.A: Physical construction of roads and buildings
options.B: Development or installation of technological systems
options.D: Improvement of community welfare through social programmes

questions.explanation: IT projects are defined as those involving the development or installation of technological systems - including software development, website creation, ICT centre establishment, and database management systems.

questions.stem: What does the GRPI Model stand for?
questions.explanation: GRPI represents Goals, Roles, Processes, and Interpersonal relationships[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Software development, website creation, and database management systems are examples of which project type?
questions.explanation: Software development, website creation, and database management systems are all explicitly listed as examples of IT projects - reflecting their focus on technological development and deployment.

questions.stem: What occurs during the “Storming” stage of team development?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal friction, competition, and disagreement mark the Storming phase[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Social projects are designed to:

options.A: Generate new knowledge through systematic research
options.C: Address social challenges and promote societal well-being
options.D: Expand business operations and increase profitability

questions.explanation: Social projects are defined as those that address social challenges and promote societal well-being - including poverty alleviation programmes, youth empowerment schemes, and skill acquisition training.

questions.stem: The difference between the earliest starting time and the latest starting time for all activities on the critical path is:
questions.explanation: Activities on the critical path have zero float/slack, meaning Earliest Start Time equals Latest Start Time ($LS - ES = 0$)[cite: 4, 5].

questions.stem: Poverty alleviation programmes, youth empowerment schemes, and skill acquisition training are examples of:
questions.explanation: Poverty alleviation programmes, youth empowerment schemes, and skill acquisition training are all listed as examples of social projects - initiatives focused on improving societal conditions and human welfare.

questions.stem: A project sponsor typically:
questions.explanation: The sponsor secures financial budget, advocates for the project, and offers executive guidance[cite: 2].

questions.stem: How do social projects MOST differ from community development projects based on the Week 4 lecture?

options.A: Social projects are government-funded while community development projects are privately funded
options.B: Social projects address social challenges and promote societal well-being, while community development projects focus on improving community welfare through physical and social initiatives
options.C: Social projects involve IT systems while community development projects involve construction
options.D: Social projects are short-term while community development projects have no defined end date

questions.explanation: While both types serve society, social projects specifically address social challenges (poverty, youth unemployment) whereas community development projects focus on improving community welfare through initiatives like rural electrification, boreholes, and sanitation - a distinction made by their definitions and examples in the lecture.

questions.stem: ROI (Return on Investment) in evaluation measures:
questions.explanation: ROI assesses financial returns relative to capital invested[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Government or public sector projects are defined as projects:

options.A: Owned exclusively by private entrepreneurs for profit
options.B: Financed and executed by government institutions
options.C: Carried out by international NGOs without government involvement
options.D: Funded jointly by private companies and academic institutions

questions.explanation: Government/public sector projects are defined as those financed and executed by government institutions - including public schools, healthcare facilities, transportation systems, and agricultural programmes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a method of project evaluation?
questions.explanation: While useful, post-project review was not listed among standard initial evaluation methods in this contextual framework[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a consequence of poor project selection?
questions.explanation: Waste of resources is the first consequence listed for poor project selection - alongside project failure, financial losses, poor organisational performance, and lack of community support.

questions.stem: What happens during the "Norming" stage of team development?
questions.explanation: During Norming, conflicts settle and the team establishes working agreements and shared processes[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Public school construction, healthcare facilities, and transportation systems are examples of:
questions.explanation: Public school construction, healthcare facilities, and transportation systems are explicitly listed as examples of government/public sector projects - publicly financed initiatives that serve the general population.

questions.stem: What is the focus of a feasibility study?
questions.explanation: Feasibility studies test whether a project is realistic, achievable, and practical[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a small-scale project?

options.A: High capital requirement, complex planning, and long implementation period
options.C: Limited resources, short duration, and simple management structure
options.D: Requires specialised technical expertise and has high risk involvement

questions.explanation: Small-scale projects are characterised by limited resources, short duration, and a simple management structure - making them manageable by a small team with minimal complexity.

questions.stem: Which one considers externalities like pollution?
questions.explanation: Social Cost-Benefit Analysis considers external factors like pollution that affect society as a whole[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Organisation of a departmental seminar is given as an example of which scale of project?
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly uses departmental seminar organisation as the example of a small-scale project - an activity requiring limited resources, completed in a short duration with a simple management structure.

questions.stem: Lessons learned sessions are held to:
questions.explanation: Lessons learned capture positive experience and mistakes to benefit future initiatives[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Establishment of a computer laboratory is given as an example of which scale of project?
questions.explanation: The lecture uses the establishment of a computer laboratory as the example of a medium-scale project - one requiring moderate funding and team coordination, sitting between small and large in complexity.

questions.stem: Which phase involves breaking down the project into manageable tasks?
questions.explanation: In planning, the project is decomposed into work packages, schedules, and budgets[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics is associated with large-scale projects?

options.B: Simple management structure and minimal funding
options.C: High capital requirement, complex planning, and long implementation period
options.D: Moderate funding and straightforward team coordination

questions.explanation: Large-scale projects are characterised by a high capital requirement, complex planning, and a long implementation period - as illustrated by the example of constructing a university campus.

questions.stem: Which constraint is directly impacted by resource availability?
questions.explanation: Resource availability dictates what scope can be completed, budget costs, and project duration[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Construction of a university campus is given as an example of which scale of project?
questions.explanation: The lecture uses the construction of a university campus as the example of a large-scale project - reflecting the high capital requirement, complex planning, and long implementation period that define this category.

questions.stem: When in the project life cycle is feasibility typically assessed?
questions.explanation: Feasibility is evaluated early in initiation to decide if the project should be authorized[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A project manager is comparing three projects: a departmental seminar, a computer laboratory, and a university campus construction. In ascending order of scale, how should these be arranged?

options.A: University campus → computer laboratory → departmental seminar
options.B: Computer laboratory → departmental seminar → university campus
options.C: Departmental seminar → computer laboratory → university campus
options.D: Departmental seminar → university campus → computer laboratory

questions.explanation: The three examples map directly to the three project scales: departmental seminar (small-scale), computer laboratory (medium-scale), and university campus construction (large-scale) - ascending from simplest to most complex.

questions.stem: Formative evaluation occurs:
questions.explanation: Formative evaluation is ongoing and helps improve performance while execution is underway[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A project owned and financed by an individual entrepreneur is classified as a:
questions.explanation: Private projects are defined as those owned and financed by individuals or private organisations - distinguishing them from public projects (government-owned) and joint projects (partnership between government and private organisations).

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a standard type of feasibility study?
questions.explanation: Standard categories include technical, economic/financial, legal, operational, and schedule feasibility; emotional is not standard[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A project executed through a partnership between the government and a private construction firm is classified as a:
questions.explanation: Joint projects are defined as those executed through a partnership between government and private organisations - commonly known as Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) in project management practice.

questions.stem: Which CBA method includes spillover effects?
questions.explanation: SCBA includes indirect external benefits and spillover costs to society[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists all three categories of project classification based on ownership?
questions.explanation: The three ownership-based classifications given in Week 4 are private projects (individual/private organisation), public projects (government-funded), and joint projects (government-private partnership).

questions.stem: ________ is the discipline of planning, organizing, securing and managing resources to bring about the successful completion of specific goals and objectives.
questions.explanation: Project Management is defined as applying knowledge, tools, and techniques to plan, secure resources, and achieve specific project objectives[cite: 4].

questions.stem: A federal government hospital project is funded entirely from the national budget. Based on ownership, this is a:
questions.explanation: A project funded entirely by the government from the national budget is a public project - owned and funded by the government, as defined in the ownership-based classification.

questions.stem: Accountability in project evaluation means:
questions.explanation: Accountability ensures that responsible teams are answerable for project outcomes[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a factor influencing the choice of project type?

options.A: The personal preferences of team members
options.C: The number of competing projects in the sector
options.D: The academic qualifications of the project sponsor

questions.explanation: Availability of funds is the first factor listed as influencing the choice of project type - alongside organisational objectives, technical expertise, environmental conditions, time availability, and expected benefits.

questions.stem: A milestone in project management marks:
questions.explanation: Milestones mark key progress points or completed major phases[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which characteristic of WBS ensures that each task can be assigned to a responsible individual or team?
questions.explanation: Responsibility Assignment is the WBS characteristic that ensures each task in the structure can be assigned to a responsible individual or team, promoting accountability.

questions.stem: If a project's scope increases, what typically happens to cost and time?

options.D: Time decreases, cost stays the same

questions.explanation: Expanding work deliverables requires additional time to complete and more money to fund[cite: 3].

questions.stem: An organisation decides not to pursue a large construction project because it lacks engineers and architects. Which factor influencing project type selection does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: The absence of qualified engineers and architects reflects a deficit in technical expertise - one of the key factors that influences an organisation's choice of project type.

questions.stem: What is a disadvantage of the project life cycle?

options.B: May stifle creativity due to rigidity

questions.explanation: Strict adherence to linear phase structures can create rigidity that stifles innovation[cite: 3].

questions.stem: How many factors influencing the choice of project type are listed in the Week 4 lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture lists six factors influencing the choice of project type: availability of funds, organisational objectives, technical expertise, environmental conditions, time availability, and expected benefits.

questions.stem: What is a characteristic of the “Performing” stage in Tuckman’s model?
questions.explanation: Teams in the Performing stage display high efficiency, clear communication, and autonomous productivity[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A community chooses to implement a borehole water project rather than a solar energy scheme because it needs clean water urgently and lacks the technical capacity for solar installation. Which TWO factors are at play here?

options.A: Availability of funds and project classification

questions.explanation: The decision reflects lack of technical expertise (no capacity for solar installation) and time availability (urgent need for water means a faster-to-implement solution is preferred) - two of the six listed factors.

questions.stem: Which is NOT a strategy to manage triple constraints?
questions.explanation: Ignoring stakeholder input damages project alignment and is not a valid management strategy[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Knowledge of project types helps project managers to do all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The lecture states that knowledge of project types helps select appropriate management techniques, allocate resources effectively, identify risks early, improve planning accuracy, and enhance project success - but not to permanently eliminate all risks.

questions.stem: The project life cycle consists of:
questions.explanation: These five phases form the standard structure of a project's lifecycle[cite: 5].

questions.stem: Which benefit of understanding project types relates to directing funds, personnel, and materials to the right areas?
questions.explanation: Allocating resources effectively means directing funds, personnel, and materials to where they are most needed - a benefit made possible when a project manager understands the specific demands of each project type.

questions.stem: What does Belbin’s Team Role theory focus on?
questions.explanation: Belbin’s theory analyzes behavioral preferences and roles individuals fulfill within teams[cite: 3].

questions.stem: According to the Week 4 comparison table, what is the main objective of a research project?
questions.explanation: The lecture's comparison table states that the main objective of research projects is knowledge creation - achieved through systematic investigation, data collection, hypothesis testing, and evidence-based conclusions.

questions.stem: These are the project scope checklist EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Scope checklists consist of project objectives, deliverables, milestones, technical requirements, and limits/exclusions[cite: 4]. Non-human resources belong to resource management[cite: 4].

questions.stem: Which project type has 'infrastructure development' as its main objective according to the Week 4 comparison table?
questions.explanation: The comparison table in Week 4 states that construction projects have infrastructure development as their main objective, with a building as the representative example.

questions.stem: What happens if the initiation phase is rushed?

options.B: Risks of misalignment and failure increase

questions.explanation: Rushing initiation causes vague objectives, poor alignment, and higher likelihood of failure[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A borehole project is listed in the Week 4 comparison table as an example of which project type?
questions.explanation: The Week 4 comparison table lists a borehole project as an example of a community development project - an initiative aimed at improving community welfare.

questions.stem: Which team building model includes seven stages from Orientation to Renewal?
questions.explanation: The Drexler-Sibbet Team Performance Model maps out seven sequential stages from Orientation to Renewal[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a challenge associated with different project types in the Week 4 lecture?

options.D: Clear objectives and strong team communication

questions.explanation: Policy changes and technical difficulties are both listed among the challenges associated with different project types - alongside financial limitations, environmental challenges, and poor supervision.

questions.stem: According to team building models, when does a team typically reach peak productivity?
questions.explanation: Teams operate at optimal productivity and efficiency during the Performing stage[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A government construction project is suspended midway because a new administration changes infrastructure priorities. Which challenge does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: A change in government priorities leading to project suspension is a direct example of policy changes - one of the challenges listed in the Week 4 lecture as affecting different project types.

questions.stem: One reason for poor evaluation is:
questions.explanation: Evaluations fail or produce poor results when clear goals and objectives are absent[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A company decides to develop a new mobile banking application. Based on Week 4 classification, this is BEST described as:
questions.explanation: Developing a mobile banking application involves the development of a technological system - the defining characteristic of IT projects, which include software development, website creation, and database management systems.

questions.stem: Impact assessment examines:
questions.explanation: Impact assessment checks long-term consequences and lasting changes caused by the project[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A university student completes a final year research thesis on crop disease management. Based on project type, this is:
questions.explanation: A final year research thesis involves systematic investigation, data collection, and evidence-based conclusions - the defining features of research projects, which explicitly include undergraduate research projects and postgraduate dissertations.

questions.stem: Evaluation results are useful for:
questions.explanation: Evaluation identifies areas where key operational improvements can be made[cite: 2].

questions.stem: How many characteristics of a good WBS are identified in the lecture note?
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies five characteristics of a good WBS: Hierarchical Structure, Clear Definition of Tasks, Manageable Work Units, Comprehensive Coverage, and Responsibility Assignment.

questions.stem: How can frequent change orders impact a project?
questions.explanation: Frequent change orders disrupt ongoing work and push back delivery schedules[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following scenarios involves TWO different project types simultaneously?

options.A: A private firm builds an office complex for commercial use
options.B: A government agency develops a new agricultural programme to improve rural farming and trains farmers in modern techniques
options.C: A student submits an academic research dissertation
options.D: A company launches a new product for market expansion

questions.explanation: This scenario combines a government/public sector project (executed by a government agency) and a community development project (improving rural welfare) - demonstrating that projects can span multiple classification categories.

questions.stem: What is the final step before project closure?
questions.explanation: Deliverables must be formally accepted and handed over to clients before final closure[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Three organisations plan the following projects: (A) a departmental workshop, (B) a new hospital wing, and (C) a national highway. Classifying them by size in ascending order gives:
questions.explanation: A departmental workshop is small-scale (limited resources, short duration); a new hospital wing is medium-scale (moderate funding, team coordination); a national highway is large-scale (high capital, complex planning, long duration) - ascending from A to B to C.

questions.stem: What is the primary output of the initiation phase?
questions.explanation: An approved project charter is the definitive output authorizing project movement to planning[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which statement BEST summarises the key lesson of the Week 4 lecture on types of projects?

options.A: All projects are identical in nature and require the same management approach
options.B: Projects vary according to purpose, ownership, size, and operational area, and understanding these categories enables effective planning and management
options.C: Project classification is only relevant for large-scale government projects
options.D: The type of project has no bearing on the resources or expertise required

questions.explanation: The Week 4 summary states that projects vary according to purpose, ownership, size, and operational area, and that understanding these categories enables effective planning and management - encapsulating the core message of the entire lecture.

questions.stem: What is an example of a planning phase activity in a construction project?

options.C: Handing over keys to the client

questions.explanation: Creating a Gantt chart is a project planning activity used to schedule tasks and dependencies[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Why must a project be identified and selected before it is implemented?

options.A: To ensure the project sponsor receives maximum profit from the investment
options.B: To avoid waste of resources and ensure that only worthwhile projects are undertaken
options.C: To guarantee that the project will be completed ahead of schedule
options.D: To allow team members to choose which tasks they prefer to execute

questions.explanation: The lecture introduction states that project identification and selection help organisations avoid waste of resources and ensure that only worthwhile projects are undertaken - the core justification for the process.

questions.stem: Why is stakeholder input important in a feasibility study?

options.C: They influence project approval and direction

questions.explanation: Key stakeholders hold decision authority and provide insights that influence viability[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which two processes must occur before any project is implemented, according to the Week 6 lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture states that before any project is implemented, it must first be identified and selected - with identification recognising the need and selection determining the most viable option.

questions.stem: Who should be involved in project evaluation?
questions.explanation: Including relevant stakeholders improves evaluation accuracy, coverage, and acceptance[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Project identification is best defined as:

options.A: The process of evaluating different project proposals and choosing the most suitable one
options.B: The process of recognising and defining a project idea that addresses a particular problem or need
options.C: The systematic monitoring of ongoing project activities to ensure compliance
options.D: The final stage of project management in which completed projects are formally closed

questions.explanation: Project identification is defined as the process of recognising and defining a project idea that addresses a particular problem or need within an organisation or community - distinguishing it from project selection, which comes after.

questions.stem: Project evaluation primarily aims to:
questions.explanation: The main goal of evaluation is to measure whether a project met its intended goals[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Project identification involves:

options.A: Assigning budget allocations to approved project proposals
options.B: Generating project ideas and determining possible solutions to existing problems
options.C: Monitoring project execution to detect deviations from the plan
options.D: Formally closing projects and archiving all documentation

questions.explanation: The lecture states that project identification involves generating project ideas and determining possible solutions to existing problems - it is the creative and diagnostic stage that precedes evaluation and selection.

questions.stem: Meeting the need of customers and major stakeholders will require

options.A: Integrated project planning and control system

questions.explanation: An integrated project planning and control system ensures proper coordination, tracking, and delivery across all stakeholder requirements.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a source of project ideas in the Week 6 lecture?
questions.explanation: Community needs is the first source of project ideas listed in the lecture - alongside organisational objectives, government policies, technological development, market demand, research findings, and social problems.

questions.stem: Which tool helps teams track progress and align goals?
questions.explanation: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) measure progress against target goals[cite: 3].

questions.stem: How many sources of project ideas are identified in the Week 6 lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture lists seven sources of project ideas: community needs, organisational objectives, government policies, technological development, market demand, research findings, and social problems.

questions.stem: If a project's budget is reduced by 20%, which two constraints are most affected?
questions.explanation: Cutting budget generally forces cuts to deliverables (scope) or compromises standard quality[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A government announces a new policy requiring all secondary schools to establish computer laboratories. An education NGO uses this announcement to generate a project idea. Which source of project ideas does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Using a government policy announcement as the basis for generating a project idea reflects the 'government policies' source - one of the seven listed sources of project ideas in the lecture.

questions.stem: One goal of the commercial cost-benefit analysis (CCBA) is:
questions.explanation: Commercial Cost-Benefit Analysis (CCBA) measures a project's financial returns and commercial profitability[cite: 2].

questions.stem: A researcher publishes a study showing that poor sanitation causes 60% of illnesses in a community. A development organisation uses this finding to propose a sanitation project. Which source of project ideas does this represent?
questions.explanation: Using published research data to generate a project idea reflects the 'research findings' source - project ideas can emerge from academic or field research that identifies gaps, needs, or opportunities.

questions.stem: Which phase typically requires the most resources (time, money, personnel)?
questions.explanation: Execution consumes the vast majority of resources as physical deliverables are actually produced[cite: 3].

questions.stem: An entrepreneur notices that online shopping has become popular and decides to develop a logistics app to meet delivery demands. Which source of project ideas applies here?
questions.explanation: Responding to growing demand for delivery services by developing a logistics application reflects the 'market demand' source of project ideas - identifying and addressing an unmet need in the marketplace.

questions.stem: What provides evidence of project effectiveness?
questions.explanation: A formal evaluation report summarizes findings and proves whether goals were met[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists ALL seven sources of project ideas from the Week 6 lecture?

options.A: Community needs, organisational objectives, government policies, technological development, market demand, research findings, social problems
options.B: Community needs, feasibility studies, government budgets, market surveys, technical reports, social audits, project proposals
options.C: Organisational objectives, stakeholder preferences, expert judgment, cost analysis, risk assessment, project goals, time constraints
options.D: Market demand, project scope, technological development, community needs, budget reports, social policies, team skills

questions.explanation: The seven sources listed in the lecture are: community needs, organisational objectives, government policies, technological development, market demand, research findings, and social problems - all captured only in the first option.

questions.stem: Which tool is used for qualitative evaluation?
questions.explanation: Surveys and interviews collect qualitative feedback, opinions, and observations[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as an importance of project identification?

options.A: Guarantees zero financial loss on all projects
options.C: Eliminates the need for a feasibility study
options.D: Ensures that all identified projects are implemented

questions.explanation: One of the stated importances of project identification is that it helps align projects with organisational goals - ensuring that proposed projects are relevant to the organisation's mission and strategic direction.

questions.stem: What does a pre-project evaluation involve?
questions.explanation: Pre-project evaluation checks project feasibility and viability prior to starting execution[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Project identification improves decision-making in project planning primarily by:

options.A: Assigning team members to tasks before objectives are defined
options.B: Recognising development needs and providing solutions to existing problems
options.C: Setting a budget before identifying what the project is meant to achieve
options.D: Selecting the project with the lowest cost regardless of its benefits

questions.explanation: Project identification improves decision-making by recognising development needs and providing solutions to existing problems - giving decision-makers a clear, evidence-based foundation for choosing which projects to pursue.

questions.stem: What is a typical outcome of a feasibility study?
questions.explanation: Feasibility studies provide the necessary evidence for leadership to make a Go/No-Go decision[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which pair of importances of project identification is correctly stated?

options.A: Guarantees project profit and eliminates all risks
options.B: Recognises development needs and generates useful project ideas
options.C: Replaces the need for project selection and ensures automatic funding
options.D: Speeds up project execution and reduces team size

questions.explanation: The lecture lists recognising development needs and generating useful project ideas as two of the five stated importances of project identification - both are core outputs of a well-conducted identification process.

questions.stem: Project evaluation helps to:
questions.explanation: Evaluation equips management with facts and insight needed for sound decision-making[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Project selection is best defined as:

options.A: The process of recognising and defining a project idea that addresses a particular problem
options.B: The process of evaluating different project proposals and choosing the most suitable project based on available resources and expected benefits
options.C: The formal documentation of completed project activities and outcomes
options.D: The assignment of roles and responsibilities to project team members

questions.explanation: Project selection is defined as the process of evaluating different project proposals and choosing the most suitable project to implement based on available resources and expected benefits - it follows project identification and narrows down the options.

questions.stem: Which of these arrangements is appropriate for an organization that has both standard process and product?
questions.explanation: A matrix structure balances functional expertise (standard process) with project/product delivery needs[cite: 4].

questions.stem: Why is project selection necessary according to the Week 6 lecture?

options.A: Because all identified projects must be implemented simultaneously
options.B: Because resources are usually limited and not all identified projects can be implemented
options.C: Because project sponsors always fund only one type of project
options.D: Because project managers are only qualified to handle one project at a time

questions.explanation: The lecture states that since resources are usually limited, not all identified projects can be implemented - therefore, project selection helps in choosing the most feasible and beneficial option from the available alternatives.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a primary objective of project appraisal?
questions.explanation: Project appraisal focuses objectively on evaluating whether a project is viable, feasible, and profitable; maximizing individual stakeholder goals is not its primary function.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct description of 'feasibility' as a criterion for project selection?

options.A: The project must generate maximum profit for investors
options.B: The project must be practical and achievable
options.C: The project must be completed within one financial year
options.D: The project must be endorsed by all community members

questions.explanation: Feasibility as a project selection criterion means the project must be practical and achievable - it should be possible to execute given the available conditions, resources, and constraints.

questions.stem: A responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) defines:

options.A: Who does what in the project

questions.explanation: A RAM (such as a RACI chart) assigns individual roles and responsibilities to project activities[cite: 2].

questions.stem: An organisation rejects a project proposal because it does not align with the company's strategic goals. Which selection criterion was applied?
questions.explanation: Rejecting a project because it does not align with the organisation's strategic goals reflects the 'organisational objectives' criterion - the project must align with the goals of the organisation to be selected.

questions.stem: Which element is NOT part of the GRPI team effectiveness model?
questions.explanation: GRPI stands for Goals, Roles, Processes (Procedures), and Interpersonal relationships[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A proposed project is rejected because the organisation lacks the engineers and software developers needed to execute it. Which criterion was used?
questions.explanation: Rejecting a project due to a lack of engineers and software developers reflects the 'technical capability' criterion - the organisation must possess the technical knowledge to execute the project for it to be selected.

questions.stem: Which pitfall can be avoided by using surveys and interviews?
questions.explanation: Employing multiple data collection tools prevents over-reliance on a single evaluation method[cite: 2].

questions.stem: Which project selection criterion ensures that the project should benefit society and be accepted by the community?
questions.explanation: Social acceptability is the criterion that states the project should benefit society and be accepted by the community - ensuring that projects are not imposed on communities that oppose or would not benefit from them.

questions.stem: What triggers the start of the initiation phase?
questions.explanation: Projects begin when an underlying business need or market opportunity is identified[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Adequate financial, human, and material resources must be available before a project is selected. Which criterion does this describe?
questions.explanation: The 'availability of resources' criterion states that adequate financial, human, and material resources must be available - without sufficient resources, a project cannot be successfully executed regardless of its potential benefits.

questions.stem: What is the first phase of the project life cycle?
questions.explanation: The initiation phase begins the project, establishing objectives and feasibility[cite: 3].

questions.stem: The criterion that requires a project to provide economic benefits or value is known as:
questions.explanation: Economic viability is the criterion that states a project should provide economic benefits or value - ensuring that the financial return or economic impact justifies the investment of resources.

questions.stem: What happens during the monitoring and controlling phase?

options.B: Performance is tracked against the plan

questions.explanation: This phase ensures that the project stays aligned with the plan by tracking performance[cite: 3].

questions.stem: An organisation selects a project only after confirming it can be completed within its approved two-year implementation window. Which criterion was applied?
questions.explanation: The 'time requirement' criterion states that the project must be achievable within the available time - confirming that the project fits within the two-year implementation window before selection.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT typically part of project initiation?
questions.explanation: Developing detailed work packages happens during planning, not initiation[cite: 3].

questions.stem: How many criteria for project selection are identified in the Week 6 lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies seven criteria for project selection: feasibility, availability of resources, economic viability, organisational objectives, technical capability, time requirement, and social acceptability.

questions.stem: During execution, what is the primary role of the project manager?
questions.explanation: During execution, the PM's focus is on coordinating resources, team tasks, and workflow[cite: 3].

questions.stem: A community rejects a proposed industrial waste processing plant despite its economic benefits because residents fear health hazards. Which selection criterion is the community applying?
questions.explanation: The community's rejection based on health concerns reflects the 'social acceptability' criterion - even an economically viable project must benefit and be accepted by the community to pass this criterion.

questions.stem: What is the impact of unrealistic time estimates?
questions.explanation: Setting overly optimistic or aggressive time targets results in schedule slippage[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Cost-benefit analysis as a method of project selection involves:

options.A: Assigning scores to each project based on predetermined criteria
options.B: Comparing the expected costs of a project with the anticipated benefits
options.C: Consulting experts to recommend the most suitable project
options.D: Examining the practicality of a project before implementation

questions.explanation: Cost-benefit analysis is defined as the method that compares the expected costs of a project with the anticipated benefits - if benefits exceed costs, the project may be accepted.

questions.stem: What is an example of a deliverable in the initiation phase?
questions.explanation: The charter is a key document generated during initiation[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Under cost-benefit analysis, a project is likely to be accepted when:

options.B: Benefits and costs are exactly equal
options.D: The project has the lowest cost among all alternatives

questions.explanation: The lecture states that under cost-benefit analysis, if benefits exceed costs, the project may be accepted - this positive net benefit signals that the project is worth investing in.

questions.stem: How does poor communication contribute to project delays?

options.D: By making the project finish early

questions.explanation: Poor communication leads to mistakes, scope misunderstandings, and costly rework[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which method of project selection examines the practicality of a proposed project before implementation?
questions.explanation: A feasibility study is the method that examines the practicality of a proposed project before implementation - assessing whether it is technically, financially, operationally, and economically viable.

questions.stem: According to Lencioni’s Model, what is the foundation of team success?
questions.explanation: Vulnerability-based trust forms the base pyramid layer in Patrick Lencioni's model[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a type of feasibility in the Week 6 lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture lists four types of feasibility: technical, financial, operational, and economic. Political feasibility is not among the types identified in the Week 6 lecture.

questions.stem: ________ is a bar chart that schematically shows the relationship of activities over some time period.
questions.explanation: A Gantt chart represents activity schedules and time spans visually using horizontal bars[cite: 4].

questions.stem: A panel of engineers and economists reviews three project proposals and recommends the most suitable one for implementation. Which method of project selection is being used?
questions.explanation: Having experts or professionals evaluate project proposals and recommend the most suitable option is the 'expert judgment' method of project selection - leveraging specialised knowledge to guide the decision.

questions.stem: Lessons learned sessions aim to:
questions.explanation: Lessons learned document insights so future projects perform better[cite: 2].

questions.stem: In the scoring model method of project selection, the project chosen is:

options.A: The one with the lowest total project cost
options.B: The one recommended by the project sponsor regardless of score
options.C: The one with the highest score based on predetermined criteria
options.D: The one that takes the shortest time to complete

questions.explanation: The scoring model evaluates projects based on predetermined criteria, assigns scores to each project, and selects the project with the highest score - providing a structured, objective basis for the selection decision.

questions.stem: Which feasibility aspect examines technological requirements?
questions.explanation: Technical feasibility checks if required hardware, software, or technical expertise is available[cite: 3].

questions.stem: An organisation evaluates four project proposals using a checklist of criteria such as cost, impact, feasibility, and alignment with goals, assigning numerical values to each. The proposal scoring 87 out of 100 is selected. Which method was used?
questions.explanation: Evaluating projects using a checklist of criteria and assigning numerical scores, then selecting the highest scorer, is the scoring model method - a structured quantitative approach to project selection.

questions.stem: Assigning responsibilities, allocating resources, monitoring and controlling is reason to use
questions.explanation: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) provides the structural framework for organizing project work packages, making it easier to assign responsibilities, allocate resources, and monitor progress.

questions.stem: Which type of feasibility assesses whether an organisation has the technical knowledge and equipment to execute a proposed project?
questions.explanation: Technical feasibility evaluates whether the organisation possesses the technical knowledge, tools, and equipment necessary to execute the project - corresponding to the 'technical capability' selection criterion.

questions.stem: One distinguishing factor of Critical Path Method is that it is:
questions.explanation: CPM uses single, fixed duration estimates (deterministic), whereas PERT uses probabilistic 3-point estimates[cite: 4, 5].

questions.stem: An organisation assesses whether it has sufficient funds to finance a proposed project from start to finish. This assessment is an example of:
questions.explanation: Financial feasibility examines whether sufficient funds are available to finance the project throughout its lifecycle - a critical check before committing to implementation.

questions.stem: Which deliverable is associated with the closing phase?
questions.explanation: Capturing reflections and recording lessons learned occurs during project closure[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Economic feasibility in project selection is concerned with:

options.A: Whether the project can be delivered using existing technical systems
options.B: Whether the project will generate sufficient economic value or benefit to justify the investment
options.C: Whether the project team has the operational capacity to manage day-to-day activities
options.D: Whether the project can be funded through internal reserves

questions.explanation: Economic feasibility assesses whether the project will provide sufficient economic value or return to justify the resources invested - closely related to the 'economic viability' selection criterion.

questions.stem: Which phase involves creating a project charter?
questions.explanation: Project charters are created during Initiation to authorize the project[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists the steps in project identification and selection in their proper sequence?

options.A: Feasibility study → Generation of ideas → Screening → Selection → Evaluation → Problem identification
options.B: Identification of problems → Generation of ideas → Preliminary screening → Feasibility study → Evaluation of alternatives → Selection of viable project
options.C: Selection of viable project → Evaluation of alternatives → Feasibility study → Screening → Generation of ideas → Problem identification
options.D: Generation of ideas → Problem identification → Feasibility study → Screening → Selection → Evaluation

questions.explanation: The six steps listed in the lecture follow this logical sequence: identify problems/needs → generate ideas → screen ideas → conduct feasibility study → evaluate alternatives → select the most viable project.

questions.stem: Which phase includes procurement activities?
questions.explanation: Procurement activities span planning (sourcing), execution (purchasing), and closing (contract closure)[cite: 3].

questions.stem: Preliminary screening of ideas occurs at which step of the project identification and selection process?
questions.explanation: Preliminary screening of ideas is the third step in the process - coming after the identification of problems/needs (Step 1) and the generation of project ideas (Step 2), and before the feasibility study (Step 4).

questions.stem: Which document defines project objectives and constraints?
questions.explanation: The project scope statement outlines deliverables, boundaries, objectives, and constraints[cite: 3].

questions.stem: At which step of the project identification and selection process is the most viable project finally chosen?
